XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Heddiw, dwi'n falch o roi diweddariad i’r Aelodau ac i'r Siambr ar y cynnydd ledled Cymru i wella profiadau babanod a theuluoedd sy’n derbyn gofal newyddenedigol, a hynny drwy siarter babanod Bliss. Dyma arwydd o’n hymrwymiad parhaus i wasanaethau diogel, tosturiol a theg, sy’n canolbwyntio ar deuluoedd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Dirprwy Lywydd. Today, I am pleased to provide Members with an update on the progress being made across Wales to improve the experience of babies and families receiving neonatal care through the Bliss baby charter. This is a sign of our ongoing commitment to safe, compassionate and equitable services that are centred on families.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Each year, around 2,800 premature and sick babies in Wales receive neonatal care. For many families, admission to a neonatal unit is one of the most fraught experiences they will ever have to face. Parents may spend weeks or months in hospital dealing with daily uncertainty about their baby's health while they balance travelling to and from the hospital, their job, any other caring responsibilities they have, their family life. 

In those most difficult of circumstances, the care and support that families receive has a lasting impact. Parents need clear information, they need practical and emotional support, and they need to have meaningful opportunities to be involved in their baby's care. Parents should never be treated as visitors but as vital to the care team. Because parents know their baby. They provide comfort, reassurance and continuity, and they have an important role in those decisions about the baby's care. Supporting that relationship is at the heart of the Bliss baby charter and the principles of family integrated care.

I'm so pleased to report that all neonatal units in Wales are now engaged with the charter, either having achieved bronze accreditation or more, or submitted themselves for assessment. The charter is a practical programme that helps services place babies and families at the heart of units. It supports parents to participate in ways that reflect their circumstances and wishes, including hands-on care, involvement in decisions, accessible information and help to remain close to their baby. The charter is not simply about achieving an accreditation award. It gives a structured framework for neonatal teams to recognise good practice, to identify gaps and to agree practical actions for improvement. It encourages services to use families' experiences to shape care and support.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Bob blwyddyn, mae tua 2,800 o fabanod cynamserol a sâl yng Nghymru yn derbyn gofal newyddenedigol. I lawer o deuluoedd, mae mynd i uned newyddenedigol yn un o'r profiadau mwyaf anodd y bydd yn rhaid iddyn nhw ei wynebu fyth. Gall rhieni dreulio wythnosau neu fisoedd yn yr ysbyty yn delio ag ansicrwydd dyddiol am iechyd eu babi wrth iddyn nhw gydbwyso teithio i'r ysbyty ac oddi yno, eu swydd, unrhyw gyfrifoldebau gofalu eraill sydd ganddyn nhw, eu bywyd teuluol.

Yn yr amgylchiadau mwyaf anodd, mae'r gofal a'r gefnogaeth y mae teuluoedd yn eu derbyn yn cael effaith barhaol. Mae angen gwybodaeth glir ar rieni, mae angen cymorth ymarferol ac emosiynol arnyn nhw, ac mae angen iddyn nhw gael cyfleoedd ystyrlon i fod yn rhan o ofal eu babi. Ni ddylid byth trin rhieni fel ymwelwyr ond fel rhai hanfodol i'r tîm gofal. Oherwydd bod rhieni yn adnabod eu babi. Maen nhw'n darparu cysur, sicrwydd a pharhad, ac mae ganddyn nhw swyddogaeth bwysig yn y penderfyniadau hynny am ofal y babi. Mae cefnogi'r berthynas honno wrth wraidd siarter babanod Bliss ac egwyddorion gofal integredig teuluol.

Rwy'n falch iawn o adrodd bod pob uned newyddenedigol yng Nghymru bellach yn ymwneud â'r siarter, naill ai ar ôl ennill achrediad efydd neu fwy, neu wedi cyflwyno eu hunain i'w hasesu. Mae'r siarter yn rhaglen ymarferol sy'n helpu gwasanaethau i roi babanod a theuluoedd wrth galon unedau. Mae'n cefnogi rhieni i gymryd rhan mewn ffyrdd sy'n adlewyrchu eu hamgylchiadau a'u dymuniadau, gan gynnwys gofal ymarferol, cymryd rhan mewn penderfyniadau, gwybodaeth hygyrch a helpu i aros yn agos at eu babi. Nid yw'r siarter yn ymwneud â chyflawni dyfarniad achrediad yn unig. Mae'n rhoi fframwaith strwythuredig i dimau newyddenedigol gydnabod arferion da, nodi bylchau a chytuno ar gamau gweithredu ymarferol ar gyfer gwella. Mae'n annog gwasanaethau i ddefnyddio profiadau teuluoedd i lywio gofal a chymorth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Ym mis Medi 2025, fe wnaeth Llywodraeth Cymru roi bron i £100,000 i Bliss ar gyfer sefydlu rhaglen gwella gwasanaethau newyddenedigol genedlaethol i Gymru. Ers hynny, mae pob uned newyddenedigol naill ai wedi cyflawni achrediad lefel efydd neu wedi cyflwyno tystiolaeth i’w hasesu o dan siarter babanod Bliss. Mae hon yn garreg filltir bwysig i’r gwasanaethau hyn yng Nghymru. Ond nid dyna ddiwedd yr hanes. Rydyn ni wedi gweld rhagor o gynnydd eto: mae un uned wedi cyflawni achrediad lefel arian yn barod, ac mae tair uned arall yn paratoi i gyflwyno cais am asesiad ar y lefel hon. Felly, mae ymrwymiad ein timau i wella’n barhaus yn gwbl amlwg. Maen nhw’n awyddus i sicrhau bod babanod a theuluoedd sy’n derbyn gofal ganddyn nhw yn cael profiad gwell. 

Dros y flwyddyn ddiwethaf, mae Bliss wedi gweithio’n uniongyrchol gyda thimau mewn unedau dros Gymru gyfan. Mae unedau wedi cael cymorth i asesu eu sefyllfa yn erbyn safonau’r siarter, i gynnal adolygiadau ac archwiliadau, i nodi blaenoriaethau lleol, ac i ddatblygu camau ar gyfer gwella. Diolch i’r rhaglen, mae gan wasanaethau gyfle hefyd i rannu arferion da a’r hyn y maen nhw wedi ei ddysgu ar hyd y daith.

Nawr, dyw pob uned ddim yn union yr un fath. Maen nhw’n amrywio o ran eu maint, maen nhw'n amrywio o ran y ddarpariaeth arbenigol sy’n cael ei chynnig ganddyn nhw, ac o ran eu cyfleusterau a’u hadnoddau, a’u staff. Maen nhw hefyd yn gwasanaethu gwahanol gymunedau. Mae’r siarter yn gosod uchelgais genedlaethol i bob uned ar y cyd, ond mae hi hefyd yn caniatáu i bob gwasanaeth yn unigol ganolbwyntio ar newidiadau a fydd yn gwneud y gwahaniaeth mwyaf yn lleol.

Ni fyddai hyn yn bosibl heb ymroddiad staff yr unedau newyddenedigol ledled Cymru, a hoffwn i dalu teyrnged i ymrwymiad a gwaith caled y staff hynny. Bydd cyflawni’r rhaglen hon yn gofyn am arweinyddiaeth ac ymgysylltu parhaus, ochr yn ochr â’r pwysau dyddiol sy’n gysylltiedig â darparu gofal arbenigol. Mae nyrsys, meddygon, gweithwyr proffesiynol perthynol i iechyd, seicolegwyr, gweithwyr cymorth ac eraill yn gweithio gyda’i gilydd i roi mwy o bwyslais ar gynnwys teuluoedd wrth ddatblygu’r ddarpariaeth, a gwneud gwelliannau ystyrlon i ofal.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
In September 2025, the Welsh Government provided almost £100,000 to Bliss to establish a national neonatal service improvement programme for Wales. Since then, every neonatal unit has either achieved bronze-level accreditation or submitted evidence for assessment under the Bliss baby charter. This marks an important milestone for these services in Wales. However, that is not the end of the story. We have seen further progress: one unit has already achieved silver-level accreditation, and three other units are preparing to submit applications for assessment at this level. Therefore, the commitment of our teams to continuous improvement is abundantly clear. They are keen to ensure that the babies and families receiving their care have a better experience.

Over the past year, Bliss has worked directly with teams in neonatal units across Wales. Units have received support to assess their position against the charter's standards, to carry out reviews and audits, identify local priorities, and develop actions for improvement. Thanks to the programme, services also have the opportunity to share good practice and lessons learned along the way.

Now, not every unit is exactly the same. They vary in size, they vary in the specialist services they provide, and in their facilities, resources, and their staff. They also serve different communities. The charter sets out a national ambition for all units, a shared national ambition, and, at the same time, it allows each individual service to focus on the changes that will make the greatest difference locally.

This would not be possible without the commitment of staff in these units across Wales, and I'd like to pay tribute to the commitment and hard work of those members of staff. Achievement of this programme requires strong leadership and continuous engagement, alongside the daily pressures associated with providing specialist care. Nurses, doctors, allied health professionals, psychologists, support workers and others are working together to place a greater emphasis on including and involving families in the development of services, and delivering meaningful improvements to care.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: And we know, of course, that some parents will face additional barriers to being close to or involved in their baby’s care. These could include distance from their home, financial pressures, work, other caring responsibilities, language and communication needs, disability or difficulties in accessing accommodation and practical support. Equity is therefore central to the national programme. Bliss is developing bilingual resources, improving access to information and support for families in Wales, with particular attention to minority ethnic communities and areas of socioeconomic disadvantage. This will help services consider not only whether support is available, but whether every family can understand, can access and can benefit from that support.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ac rydym ni'n gwybod, wrth gwrs, y bydd rhai rhieni yn wynebu rhwystrau ychwanegol i fod yn agos at eu babi neu i fod â rhan yn ei ofal. Gallai'r rhain gynnwys pellter o'u cartref, pwysau ariannol, gwaith, cyfrifoldebau gofalu eraill, anghenion iaith a chyfathrebu, anabledd neu anawsterau wrth gael mynediad at lety a chymorth ymarferol. Felly, mae tegwch yn ganolog i'r rhaglen genedlaethol. Mae Bliss yn datblygu adnoddau dwyieithog, gan wella mynediad at wybodaeth a chymorth i deuluoedd yng Nghymru, gyda sylw arbennig i gymunedau ethnig lleiafrifol ac ardaloedd o anfantais economaidd-gymdeithasol. Bydd hyn yn helpu gwasanaethau i ystyried nid yn unig a yw cymorth ar gael, ond a all pob teulu ddeall, cael mynediad at y cymorth hwnnw ac elwa ohono.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mae siarter babanod Bliss yn cefnogi’r datganiad ansawdd ar gyfer gwasanaethau mamolaeth a newyddenedigol. Hwn sydd yn amlinellu ein gweledigaeth genedlaethol, sef darparu gofal diogel a theg sy’n canolbwyntio ar yr unigolyn. Argymhelliad y datganiad ansawdd yw y dylai byrddau iechyd ddilyn safonau’r siarter. Mae hefyd yn cydnabod bod gwrando ar brofiadau teuluoedd, a’u cynnwys, yn gwbl sylfaenol i sicrhau ansawdd a diogelwch. 

Mae’r gwelliannau sy’n deillio o’r rhaglen hon yn rhan o’n hymateb ehangach, wrth gwrs, i argymhellion adroddiad 'Y llwybr tuag at ddechrau mwy diogel yng Nghymru'. Mae’r gwaith hwnnw yn cadarnhau pwysigrwydd sicrhau trefniadau arweinyddiaeth genedlaethol gyson a llywodraethiant effeithiol. Mae hefyd yn cadarnhau pa mor bwysig yw hi ein bod ni wir yn gwrando ar deuluoedd, gan barhau i ganolbwyntio ar ddiogelwch, ansawdd a thegwch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
The Bliss baby charter supports the quality statement for maternity and neonatal services. This sets out our national vision of providing safe, equitable and person-centred care. The quality statement recommends that health boards should follow the standards of the Bliss baby charter. It also recognises that listening to families' experiences, and involving them, is fundamental to ensuring quality and safety.

The improvements arising from this programme form part, of course, of our wider response to the recommendations set out in 'The path to safer beginnings in Wales' report. That work reinforces the importance of ensuring consistent national leadership arrangements and effective governance. It also confirms how important it is that we genuinely listen to families, while maintaining a strong focus on safety, quality and equity.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Now, while today is an opportunity to recognise progress, the work is not complete. Bronze accreditation is an important foundation, but accreditation must not become an end point. Lasting improvement will depend on units continuing to listen to families, to review their practices, to measure the impact of any changes, and to build on what they have achieved. We have therefore secured continued funding throughout this financial year to further embed the national programme, to support units as they progress through the charter, and to strengthen the sustainability of improvements across health boards. 

During the next phase, Bliss will continue to provide tailored support to neonatal teams and strengthen access to bilingual information for families. Lessons from the programme will build an understanding of where individual units may require further assistance to meet the needs of their local population, and where common barriers may require national action. We will continue to expect clear evidence of progress. Now, as I've said, success cannot be judged solely by whether accreditation is awarded. It must be seen and felt in the experiences of babies and families—whether parents feel welcomed, informed and respected on the ward, whether they can participate in their baby’s care, and whether services listen and respond when families point out that things need to change.

I am really grateful to Bliss for their partnership and their expertise, and to neonatal teams across Wales for their ongoing commitment. Most importantly, though, I thank the parents and families who've shared their experiences and helped to shape this programme for the sake of other families in the future. Their honesty and insight have been invaluable, so too has been their bravery. I am indebted to them and I thank them.

Dirprwy Lywydd, every baby that is born prematurely or is unwell when they’re born deserves the best possible care, and every family deserves to be treated with dignity and compassion. The progress being seen through the Bliss baby charter shows what can be achieved when families, clinicians, health boards, the third sector and Government work together with a shared purpose. Now, we remain committed to supporting neonatal services across Wales to continue this journey to deliver the highest standards of care. Our ambition is clear that neonatal services in Wales should be clinically safe and effective, compassionate and equitable, and genuinely designed around the needs of babies and their families. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Nawr, er bod heddiw yn gyfle i gydnabod cynnydd, nid yw'r gwaith wedi'i gwblhau. Mae achrediad efydd yn sylfaen bwysig, ond ni ddylai achrediad fod yn bwynt terfynol. Bydd gwelliant parhaol yn dibynnu ar unedau yn parhau i wrando ar deuluoedd, i adolygu eu harferion, i fesur effaith unrhyw newidiadau, ac i adeiladu ar yr hyn maen nhw wedi'i gyflawni. Felly, rydym ni wedi sicrhau cyllid parhaus trwy gydol y flwyddyn ariannol hon i ymgorffori'r rhaglen genedlaethol ymhellach, i gefnogi unedau wrth iddyn nhw symud ymlaen drwy'r siarter, ac i gryfhau cynaliadwyedd gwelliannau ar draws byrddau iechyd.

Yn ystod y cam nesaf, bydd Bliss yn parhau i ddarparu cymorth wedi'i deilwra i dimau newyddenedigol a chryfhau mynediad at wybodaeth ddwyieithog i deuluoedd. Bydd gwersi o'r rhaglen yn meithrin dealltwriaeth o ble y gallai unedau unigol fod angen cymorth pellach i ddiwallu anghenion eu poblogaeth leol, a lle gall rhwystrau cyffredin fod angen gweithredu cenedlaethol. Byddwn yn parhau i ddisgwyl tystiolaeth glir o gynnydd. Nawr, fel rydw i wedi dweud, ni ellir barnu llwyddiant yn unig yn ôl a yw achrediad yn cael ei ddyfarnu. Rhaid ei weld a'i deimlo ym mhrofiadau babanod a theuluoedd—p'un a yw rhieni yn teimlo eu bod yn cael eu croesawu, eu bod yn cael eu hysbysu a'u parchu ar y ward, a allan nhw gymryd rhan yng ngofal eu babi, ac a yw gwasanaethau yn gwrando ac yn ymateb pan fydd teuluoedd yn dweud bod angen i bethau newid.

Rwy'n ddiolchgar iawn i Bliss am eu partneriaeth a'u harbenigedd, ac i dimau newyddenedigol ledled Cymru am eu hymrwymiad parhaus. Yn bwysicaf oll, fodd bynnag, diolchaf i'r rhieni a'r teuluoedd sydd wedi rhannu eu profiadau ac wedi helpu i lunio'r rhaglen hon er lles teuluoedd eraill yn y dyfodol. Mae eu gonestrwydd a'u dirnadaeth wedi bod yn amhrisiadwy, felly hefyd eu dewrder. Rwy'n ddyledus iddyn nhw ac rwy'n diolch iddyn nhw.

Ddirprwy Lywydd, mae pob babi sy'n cael ei eni yn gynamserol neu sy'n sâl pan gaiff ei eni yn haeddu'r gofal gorau posibl, ac mae pob teulu yn haeddu cael ei drin gydag urddas a thosturi. Mae'r cynnydd sy'n cael ei weld trwy siarter babanod Bliss yn dangos beth y gellir ei gyflawni pan fydd teuluoedd, clinigwyr, byrddau iechyd, y trydydd sector a'r Llywodraeth yn gweithio gyda'i gilydd i'r un perwyl. Nawr, rydym ni'n parhau i fod yn ymrwymedig i gefnogi gwasanaethau newyddenedigol ledled Cymru i barhau â'r daith hon i ddarparu'r safonau gofal uchaf. Mae ein huchelgais yn glir y dylai gwasanaethau newyddenedigol yng Nghymru fod yn glinigol ddiogel ac effeithiol, tosturiol a theg, ac wedi'u cynllunio'n wirioneddol o amgylch anghenion babanod a'u teuluoedd. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I need to declare an interest: I have a close relative who's a hospital consultant.

I welcome the opportunity to respond to the Deputy Minister's statement today, and I acknowledge that the Minister, from previous speeches in the Chamber, values the sanctity of life and how important this is. And I want to begin by recognising the extraordinary work being carried out every day by neonatal doctors, nurses and support staff across Wales.

When a baby is born premature or seriously ill, parents find themselves in a world they never expected to enter. Instead of taking the precious baby home, they spend days, weeks, months beside an incubator. For those families, neonatal care is not simply another NHS service, it just becomes their entire world. This is why the principles behind the Bliss baby charter are so important. Family-centred care means recognising that parents are not visitors to their own babies, they are parents, and, wherever clinically possible, they should be supported to participate in baby's care and contact.

But we must make sure that today's statement represents measurable change for families rather than simply being another commitment. The Welsh Government announced funding for Bliss so that neonatal units across Wales could work towards bronze Bliss baby charter accreditation. So, my first set of questions: can you tell us exactly how many neonatal units in Wales have now achieved bronze accreditation? How many have yet to achieve it, and by what date does she expect every neonatal unit in Wales to have reached that standard? Moreover, why is it the case that out of the 14 accredited units throughout the UK, not one of top standard is located in Wales? These accredited centres elsewhere are rated gold and even platinum in some cases. For a Government that talks about ambition, where is the ambition for these little ones? Can the Minister pledge that at least one neonatal unit in Wales will become gold or above, and an accredited centre, within the term? Because families should not receive one standard of family-centred care in one part of Wales and a different standard elsewhere.

And there is another issue I believe we need to urgently address, and that is keeping families together. Bliss has highlighted the difficulties parents can face in staying overnight to be close to their sick or premature babies. Imagine giving birth, leaving the hospital without your baby, and having to travel back and fore, sometimes hundreds of miles every day, simply to be with them. And for families living significant distances from specialised neonatal care, that means travel costs, parking costs, food costs, loss of earnings and early maternity leave at precisely the moment when their sole concern should be their child. You mentioned family-centred neonatal care, but it can't simply mean telling parents they are partners in their baby's care. We have to make it practically possible for them to be there. You say in the statement you are listening and responding. So, my next question is: what specific action will the Welsh Government take to increase overnight accommodation for parents on neonatal units? And will the Deputy Minister commit to a clear national minimum standard so that, wherever possible, a parent is not forced to leave their sick and newborn child because there is nowhere for them to stay?

Finally, we need to talk about what parents experience emotionally. A neonatal admission is frightening and overwhelming. Parents need clear information. They need staff to listen to them and they need to understand what's happening to their baby and know how to participate in their care. And where they raise concerns, they need confidence that those concerns will be heard. Practices such as placing mothers on wards with mothers who've had their babies and not clearing corridors for bereaved parents have not changed since the 1960s. The Government’s recent introduction of Call for Concern into maternity and neonatal services is therefore welcome, but a system is only effective if families know it exists, staff understand it and parents genuinely feel able to use it.

And psychological support cannot be an optional extra. You said in the statement that care should be compassionate. Supporting the baby means supporting the family around that baby. So, does the Welsh Government have sufficient neonatal and psychological workforce capacity to deliver these family-centred standards consistently, and what support is being provided to units where staffing pressures are preventing progress? And will the Deputy Minister guarantee that every neonatal family in Wales has access to proper psychological support, no matter where they live, and explain how the Government will measure whether families themselves believe that the Bliss charter is actually improving the experience of neonatal care? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae angen i mi ddatgan diddordeb: Mae gen i berthynas agos sy'n feddyg ymgynghorol.

Rwy'n croesawu'r cyfle i ymateb i ddatganiad y Dirprwy Weinidog heddiw, ac rwy'n cydnabod bod y Gweinidog, o areithiau blaenorol yn y Siambr, yn gwerthfawrogi sancteiddrwydd bywyd a pha mor bwysig yw hyn. Ac fe hoffwn i ddechrau trwy gydnabod y gwaith rhyfeddol sy'n cael ei wneud bob dydd gan feddygon, nyrsys a staff cymorth newyddenedigol ledled Cymru.

Pan fydd babi yn cael ei eni yn gynamserol neu'n ddifrifol wael, mae rhieni'n canfod eu hunain mewn byd nad oedden nhw erioed wedi disgwyl bod yn rhan ohono. Yn hytrach na mynd â'r babi gwerthfawr adref, maen nhw'n treulio dyddiau, wythnosau, misoedd wrth ymyl crud cynnal. I'r teuluoedd hynny, nid yw gofal newyddenedigol yn ddim byd ond gwasanaeth arall gan y Gwasanaeth iechyd, mae'n dod yn fyd cyfan. Dyma pam mae'r egwyddorion y tu ôl i'r siarter babanod Bliss mor bwysig. Mae gofal sy'n canolbwyntio ar y teulu yn golygu cydnabod nad yw rhieni yn ymwelwyr â'u babanod eu hunain, maen nhw'n rhieni, a, lle bynnag y bo'n glinigol bosibl, dylid eu cefnogi i gymryd rhan yng ngofal a chysylltiad y babi.

Ond mae'n rhaid i ni wneud yn siŵr bod y datganiad heddiw yn cynrychioli newid mesuradwy i deuluoedd yn hytrach na dim ond bod yn ymrwymiad arall. Cyhoeddodd Llywodraeth Cymru gyllid ar gyfer Bliss fel y gallai unedau newyddenedigol ledled Cymru weithio tuag at achrediad siarter babanod Bliss efydd. Felly, fy nghyfres gyntaf o gwestiynau: allwch chi ddweud wrthym ni yn union faint o unedau newyddenedigol yng Nghymru sydd bellach wedi ennill achrediad efydd? Faint sydd eto i gyflawni hynny, ac erbyn pa ddyddiad mae hi'n disgwyl i bob uned newyddenedigol yng Nghymru fod wedi cyrraedd y safon honno? Ar ben hynny, o'r 14 uned achrededig ledled y Deyrnas Unedig, pam nad oes unrhyw rai o'r safon uchaf yng Nghymru? Mae'r canolfannau achrededig hyn mewn mannau eraill yn cael eu graddio'n aur a hyd yn oed platinwm mewn rhai achosion. I Lywodraeth sy'n siarad am uchelgais, ble mae'r uchelgais i'r rhai bach hyn? A all y Gweinidog addo y bydd o leiaf un uned newyddenedigol yng Nghymru yn dod yn aur neu uwch, ac yn ganolfan achrededig, o fewn y tymor? Oherwydd ni ddylai teuluoedd dderbyn un safon o ofal teuluol mewn un rhan o Gymru a safon wahanol mewn mannau eraill.

Ac mae yna fater arall rwy'n credu bod angen i ni fynd i'r afael ag o ar frys, a hynny yw cadw teuluoedd gyda'i gilydd. Mae Bliss wedi tynnu sylw at yr anawsterau y gall rhieni eu hwynebu wrth aros dros nos i fod yn agos at eu babanod sâl neu gynamserol. Dychmygwch roi genedigaeth, gadael yr ysbyty heb eich babi, a gorfod teithio yn ôl ac ymlaen, weithiau cannoedd o filltiroedd bob dydd, dim ond i fod gyda nhw. Ac i deuluoedd sy'n byw pellter sylweddol o ofal newyddenedigol arbenigol, mae hynny'n golygu costau teithio, costau parcio, costau bwyd, colli enillion ac absenoldeb mamolaeth cynnar ar yr union adeg pan ddylai eu plentyn fod eu hunig bryder. Fe wnaethoch chi sôn am ofal newyddenedigol teuluol, ond ni all olygu dweud wrth rieni eu bod yn bartneriaid yng ngofal eu babi. Mae'n rhaid i ni ei gwneud hi'n ymarferol bosibl iddyn nhw fod yno. Rydych chi'n dweud yn y datganiad eich bod yn gwrando ac yn ymateb. Felly, fy nghwestiwn nesaf yw: pa gamau penodol y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i gynyddu llety dros nos i rieni ar unedau newyddenedigol? Ac a fydd y Dirprwy Weinidog yn ymrwymo i safon isafswm cenedlaethol glir fel nad yw rhiant yn cael ei orfodi i adael eu plentyn sâl a newydd-anedig oherwydd nad oes lle iddyn nhw aros?

Yn olaf, mae angen i ni siarad am yr hyn y mae rhieni yn ei brofi yn emosiynol. Mae mynd i uned newyddenedigol yn frawychus ac yn llethol iawn. Mae angen gwybodaeth glir ar rieni. Mae angen staff arnyn nhw i wrando arnyn nhw ac mae angen iddyn nhw ddeall beth sy'n digwydd i'w babi a gwybod sut i gymryd rhan yn eu gofal. A lle maen nhw'n codi pryderon, mae angen hyder arnyn nhw y bydd y pryderon hynny'n cael eu clywed. Nid yw arferion fel gosod mamau ar wardiau gyda mamau sydd wedi cael eu babanod a pheidio â chlirio coridorau ar gyfer rhieni mewn profedigaeth wedi newid ers y 1960au. Felly, mae cyflwyno Galwad am Bryder yn ddiweddar gan y Llywodraeth i wasanaethau mamolaeth a newyddenedigol yn cael ei groesawu, ond mae system yn effeithiol dim ond os yw teuluoedd yn gwybod ei bod yn bodoli, staff yn ei deall a rhieni yn teimlo eu bod yn gallu ei defnyddio.

Ac ni all cefnogaeth seicolegol fod yn ychwanegiad dewisol. Fe ddywedoch chi yn y datganiad y dylai gofal fod yn dosturiol. Mae cefnogi'r babi yn golygu cefnogi'r teulu o amgylch y babi hwnnw. Felly, a oes gan Lywodraeth Cymru ddigon o weithlu newyddenedigol a seicolegol i gyflawni'r safonau teuluol hyn yn gyson, a pha gefnogaeth sy'n cael ei ddarparu i unedau lle mae pwysau staffio yn atal cynnydd? Ac a wnaiff y Dirprwy Weinidog warantu bod gan bob teulu yng Nghymru sydd â phlant mewn unedau newyddenedigol fynediad at gymorth seicolegol priodol, waeth ble maen nhw'n byw, ac egluro sut y bydd y Llywodraeth yn mesur a yw teuluoedd eu hunain yn credu bod y siarter Bliss yn gwella profiad gofal newyddenedigol mewn gwirionedd? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Catherine. Welcome to your role. The work that is being carried out in neonatal units across Wales is indeed, well, absolutely life-changing. I think it would do us all good to pause and reflect on the phenomenal work that is happening across Wales right at this moment to save babies' lives. So, thank you for highlighting that. As you said—I was struck by your phrase—it becomes their entire world, that unit, exactly. We need to be making sure that those units, the environment that families and that parents are in, are welcoming, that they are comfortable and that families feel that it's not a hindrance for them to be there, that they are central to the whole thing. How this is rolled out in different units will vary because, of course, there are lots of different reasons why there will be local considerations. But, fundamentally, it's about making sure that parents and families feel that they are part of care, and I can go through some of the practical examples of how that can be done.

You asked me about what exactly the situation is with different units, and I'm happy to provide the current position. So, all nine neonatal units in Wales are now engaged with the process, as I said. At present, Singleton Hospital and Wrexham Maelor Hospital have achieved silver accreditation. Ysbyty Gwynedd, Ysbyty Glangwili, the Princess of Wales Hospital, Prince Charles Hospital, the Grange University Hospital and Ysbyty Glan Clwyd have achieved bronze accreditation. The University Hospital of Wales in Cardiff has achieved pledge status and is working towards the bronze accreditation. Obviously, this is a staged improvement programme. You asked earlier about the possibility—and I hope that this will happen, indeed—that we will be seeing units progressing to gold and platinum status as well. That has to be our ambition, because our babies deserve nothing less than excellence in this. So, yes, I will absolutely be pushing to make sure—. Obviously, this is a matter that health boards will be monitoring, but anything that we can do nationally to be making sure that excellence is pushed for at all costs, then, yes, of course that is something that we will be very keen to look into.

You mentioned the situation across the UK and that there are other places across the UK where gold and platinum have been achieved. Of course, this is a UK-wide programme. It has developed at different rates across nations, and the flip side of it, I suppose, is the fact that all neonatal units in Wales being engaged with the programme puts us, in some ways, in a better position than other nations. But we cannot be complacent about that at all. We have to make sure that these units progress through that journey. And when a unit has had that accreditation, that doesn't mean that accreditation has to stay; they have to be continually reassessed to make sure that the improvements are continuous and that they are consistent for families.

You asked as well about keeping families together, and absolutely that is really important. I'll just share some of the practical examples of how units that have achieved the bronze accreditation and are moving further through the charter can do this. There are wards and units that have made it easier for parents to spend time with their baby with more flexible visiting arrangements, but some wards have actually introduced reclining chairs in the wards so that parents can stay as well. Absolutely, I'm really interested in the points that you made about accommodation, making that easier as well, and signposting to psychological support. All of these different components are going to be so vitally important.

You said in closing that this is only going to be effective if families know that it exists. Absolutely, because what is the point of having something that is available if it doesn't benefit the families and the parents that need it? So, we need to be making certain, and this needs to be constantly monitored to make sure that this isn't just something that is signposted, but that people know it, it's on a Post-it. It's like the Call for Concern statement that I made a couple of weeks ago now, and those two elements are going to be working together really closely too. We have to be making sure that these environments are supportive, welcoming and lead to better care, so thank you so much.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Catherine. Croeso i'ch rôl. Mae'r gwaith sy'n cael ei wneud mewn unedau newyddenedigol ledled Cymru yn wir, wel, yn newid bywydau yn llwyr. Rwy'n credu y byddai'n beth da i ni i gyd oedi a myfyrio ar y gwaith rhyfeddol sy'n digwydd ledled Cymru ar hyn o bryd i achub bywydau babanod. Felly, diolch am dynnu sylw at hynny. Fel y dywedoch chi—cefais fy nharo gan eich ymadrodd—dyna yw eu holl fyd, yr uned honno, yn union. Mae angen i ni fod yn gwneud yn siŵr bod yr unedau hynny, yr amgylchedd y mae teuluoedd a rhieni ynddo, yn groesawgar, eu bod yn gyfforddus a bod teuluoedd yn teimlo nad yw'n rhwystr iddyn nhw fod yno, eu bod yn ganolog i'r holl beth. Bydd sut mae hyn yn cael ei gyflwyno mewn gwahanol unedau yn amrywio oherwydd, wrth gwrs, mae yna lawer o wahanol resymau pam y bydd ystyriaethau lleol. Ond, yn y bôn, mae'n ymwneud â gwneud yn siŵr bod rhieni a theuluoedd yn teimlo eu bod yn rhan o ofal, ac fe allaf i sôn am rai o'r enghreifftiau ymarferol o sut y gellir gwneud hynny.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn i mi beth yn union yw'r sefyllfa gyda gwahanol unedau, ac rwy'n hapus i daflu goleuni ar y sefyllfa bresennol. Felly, mae pob un o'r naw uned newyddenedigol yng Nghymru bellach yn ymwneud â'r broses, fel y dywedais i. Ar hyn o bryd, mae Ysbyty Singleton ac Ysbyty Maelor Wrecsam wedi ennill achrediad arian. Mae Ysbyty Gwynedd, Ysbyty Glangwili, Ysbyty Tywysoges Cymru, Ysbyty'r Tywysog Siarl, Ysbyty Athrofaol y Faenor ac Ysbyty Glan Clwyd wedi ennill achrediad efydd. Mae Ysbyty Athrofaol Cymru yng Nghaerdydd wedi ennill statws addewid ac mae'n gweithio tuag at yr achrediad efydd. Yn amlwg, mae hon yn rhaglen wella fesul cam. Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn yn gynharach am y posibilrwydd—ac rwy'n gobeithio y bydd hyn yn digwydd, yn wir—y byddwn yn gweld unedau yn symud ymlaen i statws aur a phlatinwm hefyd. Dyna yw ein huchelgais, oherwydd mae ein babanod yn haeddu dim llai na rhagoriaeth yn hyn. Felly, byddaf, byddaf yn ddigamsyniol yn gwthio i wneud yn siŵr—. Yn amlwg, mae hwn yn fater y bydd byrddau iechyd yn cadw golwg arno, ond unrhyw beth y gallwn ni ei wneud yn genedlaethol i wneud yn siŵr yr anelir at ragoriaeth ym mhob achos, yna, ydy, wrth gwrs mae hynny'n rhywbeth y byddwn yn awyddus iawn i edrych arno.

Fe wnaethoch chi sôn am y sefyllfa ar draws y Deyrnas Unedig a bod yna leoedd eraill ar draws y Deyrnas Unedig lle mae dyfarniad aur a phlatinwm wedi cael eu cyflawni. Wrth gwrs, mae hon yn rhaglen ledled y Deyrnas Unedig. Mae wedi datblygu ar gyfraddau gwahanol ar draws cenhedloedd, ac ochr arall y geiniog, mae'n debyg, yw'r ffaith bod pob uned newyddenedigol yng Nghymru sy'n ymwneud â'r rhaglen yn ein rhoi ni, mewn rhai ffyrdd, mewn sefyllfa well na chenhedloedd eraill. Ond ni allwn ni fod yn hunanfodlon am hynny o gwbl. Mae'n rhaid i ni wneud yn siŵr bod yr unedau hyn yn symud ymlaen trwy'r daith honno. A phan fydd uned wedi cael yr achrediad hwnnw, nid yw hynny'n golygu bod yn rhaid i achrediad aros; mae'n rhaid eu hailasesu'n barhaus i wneud yn siŵr bod y gwelliannau yn barhaus a'u bod yn gyson i deuluoedd.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn hefyd am gadw teuluoedd gyda'i gilydd, ac mae hynny'n hollol bwysig iawn. Byddaf yn rhannu rhai o'r enghreifftiau ymarferol o sut y gall unedau sydd wedi cyflawni'r achrediad efydd ac sy'n symud ymhellach trwy'r siarter wneud hyn. Mae yna wardiau ac unedau sydd wedi ei gwneud hi'n haws i rieni dreulio amser gyda'u babi gyda threfniadau ymweld mwy hyblyg, ond mae rhai wardiau wedi cyflwyno cadeiriau gorwedd yn y wardiau fel y gall rhieni aros hefyd. Heb amheuaeth, mae gen i ddiddordeb mawr yn y pwyntiau a wnaethoch chi am lety, gwneud hynny'n haws hefyd, a chyfeirio at gymorth seicolegol. Mae'r holl elfennau gwahanol hyn yn mynd i fod mor hanfodol bwysig.

Fe ddywedoch chi wrth gloi mai dim ond os yw teuluoedd yn gwybod ei fod yn bodoli y bydd hyn yn effeithiol. Yn hollol, oherwydd pa ddiben yw hi i rywbeth fod ar gael os nad yw o fudd i'r teuluoedd a'r rhieni sydd ei angen? Felly, mae angen i ni fod yn siŵr, ac mae angen cadw golwg gyson ar hyn i wneud yn siŵr nad yw hyn yn rhywbeth sy'n ddim byd ond testun cyfeirio, ond bod pobl yn gwybod amdano, ei fod ar nodyn gludiog fel petai. Mae'n debyg i'r datganiad Galwad am Bryder a wnes i ychydig wythnosau yn ôl nawr, a bydd y ddwy elfen hynny'n gweithio'n agos iawn gyda'i gilydd hefyd. Mae'n rhaid i ni fod yn gwneud yn siŵr bod y mannau hyn yn gefnogol, yn groesawgar ac yn arwain at well gofal, felly diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd like to thank the Deputy Minister for her statement today. I know that this is something that she cares very much about. The admission of a baby to a neonatal unit is unbearably difficult and a concerning time for any family. The specialist care provided in these units helps to ensure that babies have the best possible chance of survival and quality of life, yet parents often have to put their lives on hold during this time, impacting their income, well-being and other children in their family. The charity Bliss supports parents during this time and champions the rights of premature and sick babies. 

The Bliss Wales programme was introduced with funding from the Welsh Labour Government in 2025, and I'm really glad to hear that the Deputy Minister acknowledges the important role that this has played in improving family-centred neonatal care across Wales. It's good to see that progress has been made towards the Bliss baby charter since 2025, and it's evident that funding for the whole Bliss Wales programme is now required beyond March next year.

So, Deputy Minister, you state today that funding has been secured to continue the programme through this financial year, but we know that that's only a matter of months. Parents and health professionals want to know whether the Plaid Cymru Government will fund the Bliss Wales programme after March next year. 

Whilst positive steps have been made with the Bliss baby charter, you've outlined today that the work is not complete, and my understanding is that neonatal units at the Grange and University Hospital of Wales are both at the pledge of improvement—that's the initial stage for the Bliss baby charter—and they need support to progress. Meanwhile, the other seven neonatal units, which you've mentioned, in Wales need to be able to take action to achieve the higher levels of accreditation. So, I'd be interested to know what is being doing to share that learning about the baby charter between those neonatal units to encourage the development of best practice.

Tackling health inequalities is an important aspect of this work to ensure parity in the care received by babies and families in every neonatal unit across Wales. One particular disparity faced by families has already been mentioned, and that's overnight accommodation. Parents, of course, should be able to stay with their babies at all times of day and night, but accommodation is not routinely provided. So, I'd like to know what the Welsh Government is doing to ensure that there is suitable overnight accommodation available for parents, wherever they live.

I'd also like to mention the early conversations pilot. This is separate from the Bliss baby charter, but both are part of the Bliss Wales programme. Implementation of the early conversations pilot is under way at all three neonatal units in north Wales, with further units in the south joining the pilot for its second phase. Again, funding is required to ensure parity across Wales for babies and families.

I'm glad to hear you refer to the 'The path to safer beginnings in Wales' report again in the Siambr today. That report was commissioned by the previous Welsh Labour Government, and the voices and experiences of women and families were at the centre of that assessment. So, Deputy Minister, can you give an indication of when the recommendations of the 'The path to safer beginnings in Wales' report will be fully implemented and when can we expect more clarity around delivery timelines and transparent reporting?

You'll also be aware, Deputy Minister, that the 'The path to safer beginnings in Wales' report highlighted the dedication and professionalism of the workforce in maternity services across Wales. And I know that you are also aware that the Royal College of Midwives is among those who have identified workforce capacity as the most pressing challenge currently facing maternity services in Wales. So, can the Deputy Minister provide reassurance that targeted investment in midwifery staffing, as well as improvements in workforce planning and retention, are a priority for this Government? It would also be good to know what discussions she has had with the Cabinet Minister for Health about the current situation facing midwifery graduates since the Senedd returned from recess. Babies in neonatal units require care from a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals. We also know that access to perinatal mental health and parent-infant services are vital. So, finally, will the Deputy Minister confirm today the delivery and full funding of the strategic perinatal workforce plan to ensure safe staffing levels across Wales? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe hoffwn i ddiolch i'r Dirprwy Weinidog am ei datganiad heddiw. Rwy'n gwybod bod hyn yn rhywbeth y mae hi'n poeni llawer amdano. Mae derbyn babi i uned newyddenedigol yn annioddefol o anodd ac yn amser pryderus i unrhyw deulu. Mae'r gofal arbenigol a ddarperir yn yr unedau hyn yn helpu i sicrhau bod babanod yn cael y cyfle gorau posibl o oroesi ac ansawdd bywyd, ond mae rhieni yn aml yn gorfod gohirio eu bywydau yn ystod y cyfnod hwn, gan effeithio ar eu hincwm, eu lles a phlant eraill yn eu teulu. Mae'r elusen Bliss yn cefnogi rhieni yn ystod y cyfnod hwn ac yn hyrwyddo hawliau babanod cynamserol a sâl.

Cyflwynwyd rhaglen Bliss Wales gyda chyllid gan Lywodraeth Lafur Cymru yn 2025, ac rwy'n falch iawn o glywed bod y Dirprwy Weinidog yn cydnabod y rôl bwysig y mae hyn wedi'i chwarae wrth wella gofal newyddenedigol teuluol ledled Cymru. Mae'n dda gweld bod cynnydd wedi'i wneud tuag at gyflawni amcanion siarter babanod Bliss ers 2025, ac mae'n amlwg bod angen cyllid ar gyfer rhaglen gyfan Bliss Wales y tu hwnt i fis Mawrth y flwyddyn nesaf.

Felly, Ddirprwy Weinidog, rydych chi'n dweud heddiw bod cyllid wedi'i sicrhau i barhau â'r rhaglen drwy'r flwyddyn ariannol hon, ond rydym ni'n gwybod mai dim ond mater o fisoedd yw hynny. Mae rhieni a gweithwyr iechyd proffesiynol eisiau gwybod a fydd Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru yn ariannu rhaglen Bliss Wales ar ôl mis Mawrth y flwyddyn nesaf.

Er bod camau cadarnhaol wedi'u gwneud gyda siarter babanod Bliss, rydych chi wedi amlinellu heddiw nad yw'r gwaith wedi'i gwblhau, a fy nealltwriaeth i yw bod unedau newyddenedigol yn Ysbyty'r Faenor ac Ysbyty Athrofaol Cymru ill dau ar y statws addewid o wella—dyna'r cam cychwynnol ar gyfer siarter babanod Bliss—ac mae angen cymorth arnyn nhw i symud ymlaen. Yn y cyfamser, mae angen i'r saith uned newyddenedigol arall, rydych chi wedi sôn amdanyn nhw, yng Nghymru allu cymryd camau i gyflawni'r lefelau uwch o achrediad. Felly, byddai gen i ddiddordeb gwybod beth sy'n cael ei wneud i rannu'r dysgu hwnnw am y siarter babanod rhwng yr unedau newyddenedigol hynny i annog datblygu arferion da.

Mae mynd i'r afael ag anghydraddoldebau iechyd yn agwedd bwysig ar y gwaith hwn i sicrhau cydraddoldeb yn y gofal a dderbynnir gan fabanod a theuluoedd ym mhob uned newyddenedigol ledled Cymru. Mae un gwahaniaeth penodol sy'n wynebu teuluoedd eisoes wedi'i grybwyll, a hynny yw llety dros nos. Dylai rhieni, wrth gwrs, allu aros gyda'u babanod bob amser o'r dydd a'r nos, ond nid yw llety yn cael ei ddarparu yn rheolaidd. Felly, fe hoffwn i wybod beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i sicrhau bod llety dros nos addas ar gael i rieni, ble bynnag maen nhw'n byw.

Fe hoffwn i hefyd sôn am y cynllun peilot sgyrsiau cynnar. Mae hyn ar wahân i'r siarter babanod Bliss, ond mae'r ddau yn rhan o raglen Bliss Wales. Mae gweithredu'r cynllun peilot sgyrsiau cynnar ar y gweill ym mhob un o'r tair uned newyddenedigol yng ngogledd Cymru, gydag unedau pellach yn y de yn ymuno â'r cynllun peilot ar gyfer ei ail gam. Unwaith eto, mae angen cyllid i sicrhau cydraddoldeb ledled Cymru i fabanod a theuluoedd.

Rwy'n falch o'ch clywed yn cyfeirio at yr adroddiad 'Y llwybr tuag at ddechrau mwy diogel yng Nghymru' eto yn y Siambr heddiw. Comisiynwyd yr adroddiad hwnnw gan Lywodraeth Lafur flaenorol Cymru, ac roedd lleisiau a phrofiadau menywod a theuluoedd wrth wraidd yr asesiad hwnnw. Felly, Ddirprwy Weinidog, allwch chi awgrymu pryd y bydd argymhellion yr adroddiad 'Y llwybr tuag at ddechrau mwy diogel yng Nghymru' yn cael eu gweithredu'n llawn a phryd y gallwn ni ddisgwyl mwy o eglurder ynghylch amserlenni cyflawni ac adrodd tryloyw?

Byddwch hefyd yn ymwybodol, Ddirprwy Weinidog, fod yr adroddiad 'Y llwybr tuag at ddechrau mwy diogel yng Nghymru' yn tynnu sylw at ymroddiad a phroffesiynoldeb y gweithlu mewn gwasanaethau mamolaeth ledled Cymru. Ac rwy'n gwybod eich bod hefyd yn ymwybodol bod Coleg Brenhinol y Bydwragedd ymhlith y rhai sydd wedi nodi mai capasiti'r gweithlu yw'r her fwyaf dybryd sy'n wynebu gwasanaethau mamolaeth yng Nghymru ar hyn o bryd. Felly, a all y Dirprwy Weinidog roi sicrwydd bod buddsoddiad wedi'i dargedu mewn staffio bydwreigiaeth, yn ogystal â gwelliannau mewn cynllunio a chadw'r gweithlu, yn flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth hon? Byddai hefyd yn dda gwybod pa drafodaethau mae hi wedi'u cael gyda Gweinidog Iechyd y Cabinet am y sefyllfa bresennol sy'n wynebu graddedigion bydwreigiaeth ers i'r Senedd ddychwelyd o'r toriad. Mae angen gofal ar fabanod mewn unedau newyddenedigol gan dîm amlddisgyblaethol o weithwyr gofal iechyd proffesiynol. Rydym ni hefyd yn gwybod bod mynediad at iechyd meddwl amenedigol a gwasanaethau rhieni-babanod yn hanfodol. Felly, yn olaf, a wnaiff y Dirprwy Weinidog gadarnhau heddiw gyflawni'r cynllun gweithlu amenedigol strategol a'i ariannu'n llawn i sicrhau lefelau staffio diogel ledled Cymru? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Jayne, for those questions. I know this is something really close to your heart, as well. Indeed, as you say, and it is right to put that on the record again, the work that was undertaken by the previous Government on this was foundationally important here, and I'm really proud to be continuing with that work. I think it was an incredibly valuable foundation that was laid there. Of course, we want to go further than that.

You asked, firstly, about funding. Now, as I've set out, for the second year, there is £52,000 that's been provided to support the implementation of Bliss in health boards. In terms of future funding, that is being considered as part of the broader maternity, neonatal programme planning and spending decisions, and this is clearly doing a lot of really good work, so I would be very open-minded to that, indeed. And I think we as a Government would be very open-minded to it, because we are committed to supporting improvements in maternity and neonatal services. So, that is something that we're keeping under very close review.

In terms of what you had asked about different units and making sure that they're being supported to go further with the accreditation journey, that is something that absolutely has to be happening, because accreditation on its own is a milestone, but it's not an end point. And we need to make sure that it's a staged improvement programme, as I've said, and that's something that our NHS partners are going to be working really closely with different units, with different health boards on, to support that. It's something I'm going to be keeping a really close eye on as well.

In terms of accommodation, as Catherine raised as well, already, I want to be making sure that any family, regardless of their circumstances, will be able to be involved in their baby's care. So, however we can be encouraging there to be initiatives to make sure that accommodation is part of this, of course it's something I'd be really interested in being involved in. And I would implore Members, if you are aware of circumstances where that has become a barrier, please write to me about it, because I think we need to see where—. Fundamental to Bliss is seeing where the gaps are, so it's about what can be done in the units themselves, but it's also about wider provision. So, please write to me if you see that there are gaps like that that are emerging.

Thank you, as well, for talking about the early conversations pilots—something that I know, again, is really close to your heart. As I've confirmed before, we will be implementing 'The path to safer beginnings in Wales' report's recommendations in full and that will be over a period of time. Obviously, there are some that will have to be done at a much greater pace because of their urgency, but each of those recommendations are going to be implemented in full.

You asked about the situation with midwifery, and I really recognise the significant workforce pressures that are being experienced across midwifery, maternity, neonatal and wider children's services. This is something that the Cabinet Minister and I, each of us, are really concerned about, and it is weighing heavily on us. We are encouraging health boards to maximise all opportunities, because, of course, we expect health boards to take all reasonable steps to maintain safe standards, to support staff, to ensure that workforce planning arrangements respond to current and future service needs. It's something that we are keeping under really close review.

Finally, thank you for raising perinatal mental health. It's something that was very, very close to the heart of my predecessor in this role, Steffan Lewis. Again, if you or other Members are—. It's something I'm really passionate about, making sure that the support is there for mothers across Wales, so if you are noticing any gaps in provision, please write to me so that we can arrange— .  And I make that offer, please, to Members across the Chamber, because it's something that we have to get right. Diolch, Jayne.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Jayne, am y cwestiynau hynny. Rwy'n gwybod bod hyn yn rhywbeth sy'n agos iawn at eich calon chi hefyd. Yn wir, fel y dywedwch chi, ac mae'n iawn rhoi hynny ar y cofnod eto, roedd y gwaith a wnaed gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol ar hyn yn sylfaenol bwysig yma, ac rwy'n falch iawn o fod yn parhau â'r gwaith hwnnw. Rwy'n credu ei fod yn sylfaen hynod werthfawr a osodwyd yn y fan yna. Wrth gwrs, rydym ni eisiau mynd ymhellach na hynny.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn, yn gyntaf, am gyllid. Nawr, fel yr wyf wedi nodi, am yr ail flwyddyn, mae £52,000 wedi'i ddarparu i gefnogi'r gwaith o weithredu Bliss mewn byrddau iechyd. O ran cyllid yn y dyfodol, mae hynny'n cael ei ystyried fel rhan o'r penderfyniadau ehangach ar gynllunio rhaglenni mamolaeth, cynllunio a gwariant newyddenedigol, ac mae hyn yn amlwg yn gwneud llawer o waith da iawn, felly byddwn yn agored iawn i hynny, yn wir. Ac rwy'n credu y byddwn ni fel Llywodraeth yn agored iawn iddo, oherwydd rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i gefnogi gwelliannau mewn gwasanaethau mamolaeth a newyddenedigol. Felly, mae hynny'n rhywbeth rydym ni'n ei gadw dan adolygiad agos iawn.

O ran yr hyn roeddech chi wedi'i ofyn am wahanol unedau a gwneud yn siŵr eu bod yn cael eu cefnogi i fynd ymhellach gyda'r daith achredu, mae hynny'n rhywbeth y mae'n rhaid digwydd heb os nac oni bai, oherwydd mae achredu ar ei ben ei hun yn garreg filltir, ond nid yw'n bwynt terfynol. Ac mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr ei bod yn rhaglen wella fesul cam, fel rydw i wedi dweud, ac mae hynny'n rhywbeth y bydd ein partneriaid yn y Gwasanaeth Iechyd yn gweithio'n agos iawn gyda gwahanol unedau, gyda gwahanol fyrddau iechyd arno, i gefnogi hynny. Mae'n rhywbeth rydw i'n mynd i gadw llygad agos iawn arno hefyd.

O ran llety, fel y crybwyllodd Catherine hefyd, eisoes, mae arnaf i eisiau gwneud yn siŵr y bydd unrhyw deulu, waeth beth fo'u hamgylchiadau, yn gallu bod yn rhan o ofal eu babi. Felly, fodd bynnag, fe allwn ni fod yn annog mentrau i wneud yn siŵr bod llety yn rhan o hyn, wrth gwrs mae'n rhywbeth y byddai gen i ddiddordeb mawr bod yn rhan ohono. A byddwn yn erfyn ar Aelodau, os ydych chi'n ymwybodol o amgylchiadau lle mae hynny wedi dod yn rhwystr, ysgrifennwch ataf i amdano, oherwydd rwy'n credu bod angen i ni weld ble—. Rhan sylfaenol o Bliss yw gweld ble mae'r bylchau, felly mae'n ymwneud â'r hyn y gellir ei wneud yn yr unedau eu hunain, ond mae hefyd yn ymwneud â darpariaeth ehangach. Felly, ysgrifennwch ataf os ydych chi'n gweld bod bylchau fel yna sy'n dod i'r amlwg.

Diolch, hefyd, am siarad am y cynlluniau peilot sgyrsiau cynnar—rhywbeth rwy'n gwybod, unwaith eto, sy'n agos iawn at eich calon. Fel yr wyf wedi cadarnhau o'r blaen, byddwn yn gweithredu'n llawn argymhellion yr adroddiad 'Y llwybr tuag at ddechrau mwy diogel yng Nghymru' a bydd hynny dros gyfnod o amser. Yn amlwg, mae yna rai y bydd yn rhaid eu gwneud ar gyflymder llawer mwy oherwydd eu brys, ond caiff pob un o'r argymhellion hynny eu gweithredu'n llawn.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn am y sefyllfa gyda bydwreigiaeth, ac rwy'n cydnabod yn fawr y pwysau sylweddol ar y gweithlu ym meysydd bydwreigiaeth, mamolaeth, gofal newyddenedigol a gwasanaethau plant ehangach. Mae hyn yn rhywbeth y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet a minnau, pob un ohonom ni, yn bryderus iawn amdano, ac mae'n pwyso'n drwm arnom ni. Rydym ni'n annog byrddau iechyd i wneud y mwyaf o'r holl gyfleoedd, oherwydd, wrth gwrs, rydym ni'n disgwyl i fyrddau iechyd gymryd pob cam rhesymol i gynnal safonau diogel, i gefnogi staff, i sicrhau bod trefniadau cynllunio'r gweithlu yn ymateb i anghenion gwasanaeth nawr ac yn y dyfodol. Mae'n rhywbeth rydym ni'n ei gadw dan adolygiad agos iawn.

Yn olaf, diolch am godi iechyd meddwl amenedigol. Mae'n rhywbeth a oedd yn agos iawn, iawn at galon fy rhagflaenydd yn y rôl hon, Steffan Lewis. Unwaith eto, os ydych chi neu Aelodau eraill yn—. Mae'n rhywbeth rydw i'n angerddol iawn amdano, gwneud yn siŵr bod y gefnogaeth yno i famau ledled Cymru, felly os ydych chi'n sylwi ar unrhyw fylchau yn y ddarpariaeth, ysgrifennwch ataf i er mwyn i ni allu trefnu— . Ac rwy'n gwneud y cynnig hwnnw, os gwelwch yn dda, i Aelodau ar draws y Siambr, oherwydd mae'n rhywbeth y mae'n rhaid i ni ei wneud yn iawn. Diolch, Jayne.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Can I thank the Deputy Minister for this afternoon's statement on what is an incredibly emotive area? I welcome this statement, as we haven't really received an update on the Bliss baby charter since it was introduced in September last year. To be clear, my Welsh Conservative colleagues and I support the charter and its aims of improving outcomes for the most vulnerable babies all across Wales. I cannot even begin to imagine what it must be like for families having to navigate life with a premature or seriously ill baby. It must be incredibly frightening and difficult for so many, and so any action being taken to improve neonatal care in Wales will have our unwavering support. Parents should be treated as partners in their baby's care, properly informed and supported, and able to spend as much time with their baby as circumstances allow.

The previous Welsh Government invested £100,000 in ensuring all neonatal units in Wales are working towards the bronze level of the Bliss baby charter, and I'm pleased to hear, as per your statement, that all units have either reached or are about to, hopefully, reach bronze, with some excelling further already. Following Jayne Bryant's question about funding, I'd like to know by what date and time will funding support from this Government be put in place to help this progress further.

Deputy Minister, as we heard earlier, this year, 'The path to safer beginnings in Wales' assessment of maternity and neonatal services was published. That piece of work identified a number of issues and challenges, including poor co-ordination between units regarding cot and maternity bed availability, uncertainty around neonatal cot configuration and even provision of transitional care and delays in transport arrangements. You confirmed that this Government would implement the assessment's recommendations, but can you please elaborate on what steps this Plaid Government has already taken in this area to date?

In particular, I would be keen to hear more about the Government's plans to implement a national maternity bed and neonatal cot finder, and when families will be able to access it. The charity Bliss carried out a survey of neonatal units across Wales that found that 85 per cent of babies could not have even one parent stay in a room with them overnight. This was due to a lack of appropriate accommodation and the condition of some estates. This will have a hugely detrimental impact on this Government's ambition to deliver a more family-centred approach. So, Deputy Minister, how is this Government going to be addressing this moving forward?

Families and premature children also need support long after they have left the neonatal unit. Parents of children admitted to neonatal care are more than likely to experience mental health needs, yet less than a third of parents told the charity The Smallest Things that they received formal emotional support after having left the unit. Also, just one in five parents agree that their GP understands their or their baby's needs, and a little over a third felt that their health visitors understood their and their baby's needs.

Parents cite the lack of understanding and joined-up support between health and education. So, I'd like to know what action the Welsh Government is taking to ensure children born prematurely receive joined-up support following discharge from neonatal care, including appropriate sharing of their neonatal history between health visiting, early years and education services. How will they ensure professionals across these services understand the potential impact premature birth can have on learning and development, and are ready to identify and meet those needs? Deputy Minister, parents should be at the heart of neonatal care, and I sincerely hope with every ounce of my being that this Welsh Government gets this important piece of work right. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
A gaf i ddiolch i'r Dirprwy Weinidog am y datganiad y prynhawn yma ar yr hyn sy'n faes hynod emosiynol? Rwy'n croesawu'r datganiad hwn, gan nad ydym ni wedi derbyn diweddariad ar y siarter babanod Bliss ers ei chyflwyno ym mis Medi y llynedd. I fod yn glir, mae fy nghyd-aelodau yn y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig a minnau yn cefnogi'r siarter a'i nodau o wella canlyniadau i'r babanod mwyaf agored i niwed ledled Cymru. Ni allaf hyd yn oed ddechrau dychmygu sut beth yw hi i deuluoedd sy'n gorfod byw gyda babi cynamserol neu ddifrifol wael. Mae'n rhaid ei fod yn hynod frawychus ac anodd i gymaint o bobl, ac felly bydd unrhyw beth a wneir i wella gofal newyddenedigol yng Nghymru yn cael ein cefnogaeth ddiwyro. Dylai rhieni gael eu trin fel partneriaid yng ngofal eu babi, cael eu hysbysu a'u cefnogi'n briodol, a gallu treulio cymaint o amser gyda'u babi ag y mae amgylchiadau'n caniatáu.

Buddsoddodd Llywodraeth flaenorol Cymru  £100,000 i sicrhau bod yr holl unedau newyddenedigol yng Nghymru yn gweithio tuag at lefel efydd siarter babanod Bliss, ac rwy'n falch o glywed, yn unol â'ch datganiad, bod pob uned naill ai wedi cyrraedd neu ar fin cyrraedd efydd, gobeithio, gyda rhai yn rhagori ymhellach eisoes. Yn dilyn cwestiwn Jayne Bryant am gyllid, fe hoffwn i wybod erbyn pa ddyddiad ac amser y bydd cymorth ariannol gan y Llywodraeth hon yn cael ei roi ar waith i helpu'r cynnydd hwn ymhellach.

Ddirprwy Weinidog, fel y clywsom ni'n gynharach, eleni fe gyhoeddwyd 'Y llwybr tuag at ddechrau mwy diogel yng Nghymru', sef asesiad o wasanaethau mamolaeth a newyddenedigol. Nododd y darn hwnnw nifer o faterion a heriau, gan gynnwys cydlynu gwael rhwng unedau ynghylch argaeledd cotiau a gwelyau mamolaeth, ansicrwydd ynghylch trefniant cotiau newyddenedigol a hyd yn oed darparu gofal trosiannol ac oedi mewn trefniadau trafnidiaeth. Fe wnaethoch chi gadarnhau y byddai'r Llywodraeth hon yn gweithredu argymhellion yr asesiad, ond a allwch chi ymhelaethu ar ba gamau y mae'r Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru hon eisoes wedi'u cymryd yn y maes hwn hyd yn hyn?

Yn benodol, byddwn yn awyddus i glywed mwy am gynlluniau'r Llywodraeth i roi adnodd cenedlaethol ar waith i ddarganfod gwelyau mamolaeth a chotiau newyddenedigol, a phryd y bydd teuluoedd yn gallu cael mynediad iddo. Cynhaliodd yr elusen Bliss arolwg o unedau newyddenedigol ledled Cymru a ganfu na allai 85 y cant o fabanod gael hyd yn oed un rhiant yn aros mewn ystafell gyda nhw dros nos. Roedd hyn oherwydd diffyg llety priodol a chyflwr rhai ystadau. Bydd hyn yn cael effaith niweidiol iawn ar uchelgais y Llywodraeth hon i gyflwyno dull sy'n canolbwyntio ar y teulu. Felly, Ddirprwy Weinidog, sut fydd y Llywodraeth hon yn mynd i'r afael â hyn wrth symud ymlaen?

Mae teuluoedd a phlant cynamserol hefyd angen cymorth ymhell ar ôl iddyn nhw adael yr uned newyddenedigol. Mae rhieni plant sy'n cael eu derbyn i ofal newyddenedigol yn fwy na thebygol o brofi anghenion iechyd meddwl, ond dywedodd llai na thraean o rieni wrth yr elusen The Smallest Things eu bod wedi derbyn cefnogaeth emosiynol ffurfiol ar ôl gadael yr uned. Hefyd, dim ond un o bob pump o rieni sy'n cytuno bod eu meddyg teulu yn deall anghenion eu babi, ac ychydig dros draean sy'n teimlo bod eu hymwelwyr iechyd yn deall eu hanghenion nhw a'u babi.

Mae rhieni yn nodi'r diffyg dealltwriaeth a chefnogaeth gydweithredol rhwng iechyd ac addysg. Felly, fe hoffwn i wybod pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i sicrhau bod plant sy'n cael eu geni'n gynamserol yn derbyn cymorth ar y cyd ar ôl eu rhyddhau o ofal newyddenedigol, gan gynnwys rhannu eu hanes newyddenedigol yn briodol rhwng y gwasanaethau addysg, ymweliadau iechyd a blynyddoedd cynnar. Sut y byddant yn sicrhau bod gweithwyr proffesiynol ar draws y gwasanaethau hyn yn deall yr effaith bosibl genedigaeth gynamserol ar ddysgu a datblygiad, ac yn barod i adnabod a diwallu'r anghenion hynny? Ddirprwy Weinidog, dylai rhieni fod wrth wraidd gofal newyddenedigol, ac rwy'n gobeithio yn ddiffuant o waelod fy nghalon y bydd y Llywodraeth hon sydd gan Gymru yn gweithredu'n briodol ar y darn pwysig hwn o waith. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Natasha, and as you said at the start, it is an emotive area, and I really welcome the fact that there is cross-party support for the principles here. Of course, in terms of how it is rolled out in terms of how the accreditation progresses, all of you in the Chamber will want to be as fervently as me checking to see that that continues to progress, because this is something, as I say, we can't afford not to get right. That was an awkwardly phrased sentence, but this is something that is so important.

As you said earlier too, I can't begin to imagine what it is like. There will be people in this Chamber and there will be people watching who have been through this. It is incumbent on all of us to make sure to take every action so that some of the most difficult moments in a person's life, in a parent's life, will be filled with compassion, with love, with support, with practical actions. There's nothing that can make that magically better, but each of the—. I'll go through again some of the steps that hospitals can take in supporting skin-to-skin care, which is sometimes known as kangaroo care—I love that—it can help support bonding, improving parental confidence, contribute positively to a baby's development. It's making sure that there's support there for feeding, for comfort care, for routine care, so that when the transition happens and when a baby is able to go home, the parents can feel supported and can feel more ready and more confident that they will know what steps they need to take every day to take care of their precious baby.

In terms of communication, regular updates, you had raised again about accommodation. There's a reason why the same themes are coming up time and again. These are the things that are most vitally important to parents across Wales. We cannot afford to have a situation where families are facing these additional barriers. So, again, please, I would ask Members: when you come across examples, if there are examples of where this is not working well, please tell me, so that we can see what else can be done with this.

You asked as well about future funding. Again, it is committed for this financial year. My colleague the finance Minister is in her place. I will not incur her wrath by speculating about future budgets, but it is something that we want to take—. We need, of course, to see how this works—[Interruption.] Yes, I name-checked you there. We need to make sure that we see how this roll-out keeps progressing. Again, there will be variations in different localities. I want to empower these units to be able to keep going on this journey on their own. We need to make sure—

Diolch, Natasha, ac fel y dywedoch chi ar y dechrau, mae'n faes emosiynol, ac rwy'n croesawu'n fawr y ffaith bod cefnogaeth drawsbleidiol i'r egwyddorion yma. Wrth gwrs, o ran sut mae'n cael ei gyflwyno o ran sut mae'r achrediad yn mynd rhagddo, bydd pob un ohonoch chi yn y Siambr eisiau bod mor frwd â fi yn gwirio i weld bod hynny'n parhau i symud ymlaen, oherwydd mae hyn yn rhywbeth, fel y dywedaf, na allwn ni fforddio i beidio â'i chael yn iawn. Roedd hynny'n frawddeg lletchwith, ond mae hyn yn rhywbeth sydd mor bwysig.

Fel y dywedoch chi'n gynharach hefyd, allaf i ddim dechrau dychmygu sut beth ydyw. Bydd pobl yn y Siambr hon a bydd pobl yn gwylio sydd wedi bod trwy hyn. Mae'n ddyletswydd ar bob un ohonom ni i wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn cymryd pob cam fel y bydd rhai o'r eiliadau anoddaf ym mywyd person, ym mywyd rhiant, yn cael eu llenwi â thosturi, gyda chariad, gyda chefnogaeth, gyda gweithredoedd ymarferol. Nid oes unrhyw beth sy'n gallu gwneud hynny'n well fel ffon hud, ond mae pob un o'r—. Byddaf yn mynd trwy rai o'r camau y gall ysbytai eu cymryd i gefnogi gofal cysylltiad croen â chroen, a elwir weithiau yn ofal cangarŵ—rwy'n gwirioni ar hynny—gall helpu i gefnogi meithrin cyswllt, gwella hyder rhieni, cyfrannu'n gadarnhaol at ddatblygiad babi. Mae'n gwneud yn siŵr bod cefnogaeth yno ar gyfer bwydo, ar gyfer gofal cysur, ar gyfer gofal arferol, fel pan fydd y pontio yn digwydd a phan fydd babi yn gallu mynd adref, gall y rhieni deimlo eu bod yn cael eu cefnogi ac fe allan nhw deimlo'n fwy parod ac yn fwy hyderus y byddan nhw'n gwybod beth mae angen iddyn nhw ei wneud bob dydd i ofalu am eu babi gwerthfawr.

Felly, eto, os gwelwch yn dda, byddwn yn gofyn i'r Aelodau: pan fyddwch chi'n dod ar draws enghreifftiau, os oes enghreifftiau o ble nad yw hyn yn gweithio'n dda, dywedwch wrtha i, fel y gallwn ni weld beth arall y gellir ei wneud gyda hyn.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn hefyd am gyllid yn y dyfodol. Unwaith eto, mae wedi ei ymrwymo ar gyfer y flwyddyn ariannol hon. Mae fy nghyd-Aelod y Gweinidog Cyllid yn ei sedd. Mae angen i ni, wrth gwrs, weld sut mae hyn yn gweithio—[Torri ar draws.] Do, fe wnes i eich enwi chi yn y fan yna. Mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn gweld sut mae'r cyflwyno hwn yn parhau i symud ymlaen. Unwaith eto, bydd amrywiadau mewn gwahanol ardaloedd. Mae arnaf i eisiau grymuso'r unedau hyn i allu parhau ar y daith hon ar eu pennau eu hunain. Mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Following on from psychological support, this question will be timely. Deputy Minister, I welcome the progress being made towards the Bliss baby charter, but family-centred neonatal care can only succeed if the specialist workforce is there to support families when they need it most.

In my constituency of Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr, the experience of Chloe and her son Theo illustrates why this is so important. After Theo was admitted to neonatal intensive care in Merthyr Tydfil shortly after birth, Chloe spoke about the fear, anxiety and trauma that followed, and how those feelings stayed with her long after Theo came home.

She has said that access to specialist psychological support could have helped her process that experience and lessen its lasting impact on her family. Bliss has found a 62 per cent shortfall in neonatal allied health professionals, psychology and pharmacy staffing across Wales, with the shortfall in psychology provision standing at 90 per cent, the second highest in the UK.

Given that Cwm Taf Morgannwg health board currently has no neonatal psychologist provision in either Merthyr or Bridgend, what specific action is the Welsh Government taking to address these workforce gaps? Will you, Deputy Minister, commit to ensuring that psychological support is a central and properly funded part of delivering the Bliss baby charter in Wales? Diolch o galon.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Yn dilyn cefnogaeth seicolegol, bydd y cwestiwn hwn yn amserol. Ddirprwy Weinidog, rwy'n croesawu'r cynnydd sy'n cael ei wneud tuag at gyflawni siarter babanod Bliss, ond gall gofal newyddenedigol teuluol ddim ond gweithio os yw'r gweithlu arbenigol yno i gefnogi teuluoedd pan fydd angen hynny arnyn nhw fwyaf.

Yn fy etholaeth i, Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr, mae profiad Chloe a'i mab Theo yn dangos pam mae hyn mor bwysig. Ar ôl i Theo gael ei dderbyn i ofal dwys newyddenedigol ym Merthyr Tudful yn fuan ar ôl ei eni, siaradodd Chloe am yr ofn, y pryder a'r trawma a ddilynodd, a sut y mae'r teimladau hynny wedi aros gyda hi ymhell ar ôl i Theo ddod adref.

Mae hi wedi dweud y gallai mynediad at gymorth seicolegol arbenigol fod wedi ei helpu i brosesu'r profiad hwnnw a lleihau ei effaith barhaol ar ei theulu. Mae Bliss wedi canfod diffyg o 62 y cant o ran lefelau staffio gweithwyr iechyd newyddenedigol proffesiynol perthynol i iechyd, seicoleg a fferylliaeth ledled Cymru, gyda'r diffyg yn y ddarpariaeth seicoleg yn 90 y cant, yr ail fwyaf yn y Deyrnas Unedig.

O ystyried nad oes gan fwrdd iechyd Cwm Taf Morgannwg ddarpariaeth seicolegydd newyddenedigol ym Merthyr na Phen-y-bont ar Ogwr ar hyn o bryd, pa gamau penodol y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i fynd i'r afael â'r bylchau hyn yn y gweithlu? A wnewch chi, Ddirprwy Weinidog, ymrwymo i sicrhau bod cymorth seicolegol yn rhan ganolog ac wedi'i ariannu'n briodol o gyflawni siarter babanod Bliss yng Nghymru? Diolch o galon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Sorry, but awkwardly with the Chamber, I have to have my back to you when I'm answering you. Thank you, Sara, for sharing Chloe and Theo's story with the Chamber. We all know that neonatal admission can have that really lasting psychological effect and impact on parents and families. As has been raised by, I think, every Member so far in the Chamber, psychological support is a really vitally important component. That's why we've commissioned an independent evaluation of the Onnen service. That includes recommendations relating to neonatal workforce models and the contribution of specialist allied health professionals, including psychological services. That evaluation will help inform our understanding of current provision and future workforce requirements across Wales.

Through the Bliss baby charter, we need to be looking again—this is something that many Members have raised—at the wider needs of families, emotional well-being, and making sure that people are signposted to support. Workforce deployment, of course, remains an operational matter for health boards, but we will continue to work closely with NHS Wales, health boards and partner organisations, including Bliss, to better understand again where those gaps are, to make sure that we make the improvements that we have to and that we need to.

Mae'n ddrwg gen i, ond mae hi'n lletchwith gyda'r Siambr, mae'n rhaid i mi gael fy nghefn i chi pan fyddaf yn eich ateb chi. Diolch, Sara, am rannu stori Chloe a Theo gyda'r Siambr. Rydym ni i gyd yn gwybod y gall derbyn baban i uned newyddenedigol gael effaith seicolegol barhaol ar rieni a theuluoedd.
