XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I will declare an interest, as my family and I have been affected deeply by this very issue over the past seven days, and continue to be so. I'm sure Members would also agree with me how tragic it is that North Wales Police have been in touch with us as Members to say that a baby's body has been found on the shoreline near Bangor, in my constituency. There are calls for the mum to come forward. Please contact North Wales Police or the Betsi board. They will give you the support that you very much need at this moment in time.

I'd like to thank you, Delyth, for bringing forward the update on the Bliss baby charter, and thank every single person that's involved in trying to improve neonatal care here in Wales. The core principles are around family-centred care and are known as the seven standards, with further standards being published as we go along—specialist services and staff, benchmarking, unit information and support for families. The Bliss baby charter is now a tool that helps to examine the procedures, practices and environment of a neonatal unit. Whilst this is good, there is still a long way to go. And I have to say it now, being as I've declared an interest: I want to put on record my deep thanks, and that of my family, to Alder Hey, and to Ysbyty Gwynedd, who recognised the emergency. We need that over-the-border continuation of fantastic neonatal care.

Byddaf yn datgan diddordeb, gan fod fy nheulu a minnau wedi cael eu heffeithio'n ddwfn gan y mater hwn dros y saith diwrnod diwethaf, ac yn parhau i fod felly. Rwy'n siŵr y byddai Aelodau hefyd yn cytuno â mi pa mor drasig yw hi y bu Heddlu Gogledd Cymru mewn cysylltiad â ni fel Aelodau i ddweud bod corff babi wedi cael ei ddarganfod ar y traeth ger Bangor, yn fy etholaeth i. Mae galwadau ar y fam i ddod ymlaen. Cysylltwch â Heddlu Gogledd Cymru neu fwrdd Betsi. Byddant yn rhoi'r gefnogaeth sydd ei angen arnoch chi ar hyn o bryd.

Fe hoffwn i ddiolch i chi, Delyth, am gyflwyno'r diweddariad ar y siarter babanod Bliss, a diolch i bob person sy'n ymwneud â cheisio gwella gofal newyddenedigol yma yng Nghymru. Mae'r egwyddorion craidd yn ymwneud â gofal teuluol ac fe'u hadwaenir fel y saith safon, gyda safonau pellach yn cael eu cyhoeddi ar gyfer y dyfodol. Mae siarter babanod Bliss bellach yn offeryn sy'n helpu i archwilio gweithdrefnau, arferion ac amgylchedd uned newyddenedigol. Er bod hyn yn dda, mae ffordd bell i fynd o hyd. Mae angen y parhad trawsffiniol hwn o ofal newyddenedigol gwych arnom ni.

Janet, I am so sorry for the experience that you have just talked about in your family, and I think the thoughts of everyone in the Chamber will be with your family. I really hope everything will be all right.

You also mentioned the incredibly distressing incident that's occurred at Bangor pier. I echo what you said. It is an extremely sad, extremely distressing situation. I agree with you; in terms of Bliss, there is a long way still for us to go, of course. I am determined that we have to see continued progress. We and I will work with all health boards to do everything we can to make sure of that.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Deputy Minister. I welcome the progress being made to the Bliss baby charter today, but I particularly want to highlight the challenges faced by families in rural Wales. You have said in your statement today that individual services should focus on the changes that make the greatest difference locally. Long before the current charter programme, the neonatal team at Glangwili Hospital recognised the challenges of rurality and lack of transport, and the financial pressures facing families travelling backwards and forwards for appointments. They responded by changing the way they worked, bringing specialist appointments together to make things easier for families. Where families couldn't get to the hospital because of rurality, transport or financial pressures, the neonatal team would go out and see them at home.

You mentioned earlier what happens after they leave, which I think is just as important. They bridge the gap between hospital and home—such things as the dietician, occupational therapy, physio, speech and language. All of these are really important afterwards. They actually went on to win the Bliss project of the year award, which I think is really good for such a rural hospital. Minister, almost £1,000 was invested in this national programme in 2025. As the programme is still in its early stages, how will you make sure that good practice, like that at Glangwili, is identified, shared and implemented across Wales, rather than simply focusing on whether units meet the charter standard? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Weinidog. Rwy'n croesawu'r cynnydd sy'n cael ei wneud gyda siarter babanod Bliss heddiw, ond fe hoffwn i dynnu sylw'n arbennig at yr heriau sy'n wynebu teuluoedd yng nghefn gwlad Cymru. Rydych chi wedi dweud yn eich datganiad heddiw y dylai gwasanaethau unigol ganolbwyntio ar y newidiadau sy'n gwneud y gwahaniaeth mwyaf yn lleol. Ymhell cyn y rhaglen siarter bresennol, roedd y tîm newyddenedigol yn Ysbyty Glangwili wedi cydnabod yr heriau sy'n gysylltiedig â byw mewn ardaloedd gwledig a diffyg trafnidiaeth, yn ogystal â'r pwysau ariannol ar deuluoedd oedd yn teithio yn ôl ac ymlaen ar gyfer apwyntiadau. Bu iddyn nhw ymateb drwy newid eu ffordd o weithio, gan gydlynu apwyntiadau arbenigol i wneud pethau'n haws i deuluoedd. Pan na allai teuluoedd gyrraedd yr ysbyty oherwydd eu lleoliad gwledig, problemau trafnidiaeth neu bwysau ariannol, byddai'r tîm newyddenedigol yn mynd allan i'w gweld nhw gartref.

Fe sonioch chi yn gynharach am yr hyn sy'n digwydd ar ôl iddyn nhw adael yr ysbyty, ac rwy'n credu bod hynny yr un mor bwysig. Maen nhw'n pontio'r bwlch rhwng yr ysbyty a'r cartref—gan gynnwys gwasanaethau fel dietegydd, therapi galwedigaethol, ffisiotherapi, ac iaith a lleferydd. Mae'r rhain oll yn hynod bwysig yn y cyfnod dilynol. Yn wir, fe aethon nhw ymlaen i ennill gwobr prosiect y flwyddyn Bliss, sy'n gamp wych i ysbyty gwledig o'r fath, yn fy marn i. Weinidog, buddsoddwyd bron i £1,000 yn y rhaglen genedlaethol hon yn 2025. Gan ei bod hi'n ddyddiau cynnar o hyd ar y rhaglen, sut y byddwch chi'n sicrhau bod arfer dda, fel yr un yn Glangwili, yn cael ei adnabod, ei rannu a'i weithredu ledled Cymru, yn hytrach na chanolbwyntio'n unig ar a yw unedau'n bodloni safon y siarter? Diolch.

Diolch, Claire, for that. Indeed, in terms of the challenges that are going to be there for longer travel times for rural communities, as I said earlier, no two units will be the same, no two localities will be the same, and equity is a really important component of this, making sure that the different needs of different communities, and different communities within those communities too, are going to be addressed, and again, looking at socioeconomic disadvantage as well, looking at longer travel distances, looking at ethnic minority communities, looking at different languages, different accessibility requirements, accommodation—all of these components need to be working and need to be available to units where they're needed.

In terms of celebrating the highlights, as you have just done, I think that that is fantastic, and thank you so much for putting that on the record. We need to be making sure that, again—and this theme keeps coming up—accreditation is not an end point. The way that Bliss is structured encourages units to be progressing further through. And also, if progress isn't sustained, then accreditation can be lost. So, we need to make sure that this isn't just making sure that we get the base level of accreditation. But I want to be in a Wales where every unit is excelling, and of course that's what we should be aiming for.

Diolch, Claire, am hynny. O ran dathlu'r uchafbwyntiau, fel rydych chi newydd wneud, rwy'n credu bod hynny'n wych, a diolch yn fawr iawn am roi hynny ar gofnod. Mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr, unwaith eto—ac mae'r thema hon yn codi'n gyson—nad achrediad yw'r man terfyn. Mae'r ffordd y mae Bliss wedi'i strwythuro yn annog unedau i symud ymlaen ymhellach. A hefyd, os nad yw cynnydd yn cael ei gynnal, yna gall achrediad gael ei golli. Felly, mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr nad dim ond gwneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n cael y lefel sylfaenol o achrediad y mae hyn yn ei wneud. Ond rydw i eisiau bod mewn Cymru lle mae pob uned yn rhagori, ac wrth gwrs dyna'r hyn y ddylem fod yn anelu ato.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Lywydd, a diolch, Ddirprwy Weinidog. Hoffwn ategu geiriau'r Gweinidog a Janet Finch-Saunders ynglŷn â'r newyddion hynod o drist am farwolaeth babi ym Mangor, sy'n ergyd drom i'r gymuned leol. Dyma hefyd ddatgan buddiant, gan fy mod i am sôn ychydig am brofiad personol.

Rydw i'n croesawu'r ffocws ar ofal newyddenedigol sy'n canolbwyntio ar y teulu a'r cynnydd sydd wedi'i wneud drwy siarter fabanod Bliss. Mae'n fater personol iawn i mi. Cafodd fy mab ei eni'n gynamserol ar ôl 32 wythnos, a threuliodd bron i fis yn uned gofal arbenigol babanod Ysbyty Gwynedd. Cawsom ofal arbennig gan y staff yno, a byddaf bob amser yn ddiolchgar am hynny.

Roedd y profiad hefyd yn amlygu'r heriau y mae teuluoedd yn eu hwynebu, sy'n cynnwys fy mhartner yn dal yn gorfod gweithio yn ystod y cyfnod yna. Hefyd, oherwydd yr ôl-ofal roeddwn i'n ei dderbyn, ni chefais weld fy mab am nifer o oriau, ac roeddwn i mewn ward efo nifer o famau eraill efo'u babanod newydd, efo fy mab i mewn inciwbetor yn yr uned arbenigol.

Ond un o'r pethau pwysicaf i ni oedd cael ein cynnwys yng ngofal ein mab. Roedd y staff yn ein trin fel rhan o'r tîm o'i gwmpas, ac mae hynny'n adlewyrchu egwyddorion y siarter. Roedd hyn yn cynnwys pethau fel ein dysgu ni sut i'w fwydo fo trwy diwb, yr elfen skin-to-skin, ac mi roedd yna lety ar gael yno i ni aros, ond efallai nad oedd yr adnoddau ddim y gorau y gallen nhw fod—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much, Llywydd, and thank you, Deputy Minister. I would like to echo the words of Janet Finch-Saunders and the Deputy Minister about the very sad news about the death of a baby in Bangor, which is a great blow to the community. I would also declare an interest, as I am going to talk about my personal experience.

I welcome the focus on family-centred neonatal care and the progress that has been made to the Bliss baby charter. This is a very personal matter for me. My son was born prematurely after 32 weeks, and he spent almost a month in the infant specialist care unit at Ysbyty Gwynedd. We received exceptional care from the staff there, and I will always be grateful for that.

The experience also highlighted the challenges that families face, including my partner still having to work during that period. Also, because of the aftercare that I received, I didn't get to see my son for a number of hours, and I was in a ward with a number of other mothers with their newborns, with my son in an incubator in the specialist unit.

But one of the most important things for us was to be included in our son's care. The staff treated us as part of the team around him, and that reflects the principles of the charter. That includes things such as being able to feed him through a tube and the skin-to-skin element, and there was accommodation available there for us to stay, but maybe the resources weren't the best they could have been—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Sori. Felly, sut bydd y Llywodraeth yn sicrhau bod yr arferion gorau hyn yn cael eu rhannu a'u hymgorffori'n gyson ym mhob rhan o Gymru, a sut ydych chi'n sicrhau bod barn rhieni a'u profiadau nhw'n cael eu casglu a'u defnyddio'n rheolaidd i lywio gwelliannau pellach i wasanaethau? Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Sorry. So, how will the Government ensure that the best practices are shared and incorporated consistently in all neonatal units across Wales, and how will you ensure that the experiences and views of parents are collected and used regularly to inform further improvements to neonatal services in Wales? Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn, Mair, am rannu eich stori chi. Rydw i'n falch iawn i glywed bod y gofal roeddech chi wedi'i gael a'ch teulu wedi'i gael mor gefnogol i chi. Mae yna nifer o heriau rydych chi wedi sôn amdanyn nhw yn fanna o ran dewis iaith, o ran y ffaith roedd eich partner chi'n dal i weithio. Gallaf i ond dychmygu pa mor anodd oedd hwnna, felly dwi wir yn ddiolchgar i chi am rannu hynna gyda ni. Ond, fel roeddech chi'n dweud, pan mae hyn yn gweithio'n dda, bydd teuluoedd a rhieni yn cael eu cynnwys yng ngofal eu plentyn. Mae angen inni sicrhau bod—. Beth dŷn ni angen ei wneud yw cysoni hyn a sicrhau bod profiadau teuluoedd dros Gymru'r un mor gadarnhaol, achos bydd profiadau teuluoedd yn siapio fel mae hyn yn digwydd. Mae'n rhaid inni fod yn gwrando ar deuluoedd ac mae'n rhaid inni gymryd y feedback yna gan deuluoedd pan mae problemau'n digwydd er mwyn sicrhau bod prosesau a systemau a phobl yn dysgu o hynny, achos dylai pob teulu gael yr un gofal. Diolch, Mair.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, Mair, for sharing your own story. I'm delighted to hear that the care that you and your family received was so supportive of your needs. There are a number of challenges that you've referred to there in terms of language of choice, the way your partner had to continue to work. I can only imagine how difficult that must have been, so I'm grateful to you for sharing that with us. But, as you said, when this works well, families and parents will be included in the care of their child. We need to ensure—. What we need to do is ensure consistency in this area and ensure that the experiences of families across Wales are just as positive, because family experience will shape how this works. We have to listen to families and we have to take that feedback from families when problems occur in order to ensure that processes, systems and people learn from those experiences, because every family should have the same care. Thank you, Mair.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Deputy Minister, for most women, giving birth is supposed to be the moment when they finally hold and care for the baby they have carried for months. But, when a baby is born premature or is seriously unwell, that moment can instead mean an incubator, alarms, wires and the mother suddenly feeling that everyone else knows how to care for her baby better than she does. A mother should never feel like a visitor at her own baby's bedside.

So, I welcome the progress being made through the Bliss baby charter, because family-centred care must mean mothers and families being listened to, informed and genuinely involved in their baby's care, but Bliss themselves tell us that there are main areas of neonatal care and family support desperately needing attention. So, Deputy Minister, beyond accreditation and targets, how will you measure what really matters—whether mothers across neonatal units in Wales actually feel supported, involved and able to be a mother to their new baby?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Ddirprwy Weinidog, i'r rhan fwyaf o fenywod, rhoi genedigaeth yw'r foment, i fod, pan maen nhw'n dal ac yn gofalu am y babi maen nhw wedi'i gario ers misoedd. Ond, pan fydd babi yn cael ei eni cyn amser neu'n wirioneddol sâl, gall y foment honno olygu deorydd, larymau, gwifrau ac, yn sydyn, mae'r fam yn teimlo bod pawb arall yn gwybod sut i ofalu am ei babi yn well na hi. Ddylai mam byth deimlo fel ymwelydd wrth ochr gwely ei babi ei hun.

Felly, rwy'n croesawu'r cynnydd sy'n cael ei wneud trwy siarter babanod Bliss, oherwydd rhaid i ofal sy'n canolbwyntio ar y teulu olygu bod mamau a theuluoedd yn cael rhywun yn gwrando arnyn nhw, yn cael gwybodaeth ac yn cael eu cynnwys go iawn yn y gofal y mae eu babi yn ei gael, ond mae Bliss eu hunain yn dweud wrthym fod yna brif feysydd o ofal i fabanod newyddenedigol a chymorth i deuluoedd y mae angen rhoi sylw iddyn nhw ar frys. Felly, Ddirprwy Weinidog, y tu hwnt i achredu a thargedau, sut fyddwch chi'n mesur yr hyn sy'n wirioneddol bwysig—a yw cael mamau mewn unedau babanod newyddenedigol ledled Cymru yn teimlo eu bod yn cael cymorth, eu bod yn cael eu cynnwys a'u bod yn gallu bod yn fam i'w babi newydd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Cristiana, for that, and what you described there in terms of the expectation and the hope that every mother will have, that this will be the moment that she has dreamt of, and the gap between that and what some mothers then go through and the really desperately painful reality that they would have to face, and what Mair had described a moment ago as well, about their baby being in an incubator on another ward and being surrounded by other mothers with their own babies, and emphasising that gap. I think that the design of wards is really fundamental here, and having that compassion built into how they are designed. Absolutely, no parent should ever feel like a visitor in their child's care, in their baby's care.

As I've said earlier, this will only be deemed to be successful, by me or by anyone in this Chamber, if it leads to families feeling welcomed. And I know that's something very difficult. Of course, there are things that we can measure; they are the practical things that I've set out about how we can—. And it's very specific; I think there are more than 120 accreditation criteria that Bliss go through. But it's also about making sure that the experience of families has materially changed, that families feel part of care. So, it's, of course, about the criteria that you can put down on a piece of paper, but it's more than that too. So, thank you so much.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Cristiana, am hynny, a'r hyn y gwnaethoch chi ei ddisgrifio yn y fan yna o ran y disgwyliad a'r gobaith y bydd gan bob mam, mai dyma'r foment y mae hi wedi breuddwydio amdani, a'r bwlch rhwng hynny a'r hyn y mae rhai mamau yn mynd drwyddo wedyn a'r realiti poenus y byddai'n rhaid iddyn nhw ei wynebu, a'r hyn a ddisgrifiodd Mair ychydig funudau yn ôl hefyd, am eu babi sydd mewn deorydd ar ward arall a'u bod nhw'n cael eu hamgylchynu gan famau eraill gyda'u babanod eu hunain, ac am bwysleisio'r bwlch hwnnw. Rwy'n meddwl bod dyluniad wardiau yn gwbl sylfaenol yn hyn o beth, a bod tosturi yn cael ei ystyried wrth fynd ati i'w dylunio. Yn sicr, ni ddylai unrhyw riant byth deimlo fel ymwelydd o ran y gofal y mae ei blentyn yn ei gael, y gofal y mae ei babi yn ei gael.

Fel y dywedais i yn gynharach, dim ond os bydd hyn yn arwain at sefyllfa lle mae teuluoedd yn teimlo eu bod yn cael croeso y byddaf i neu unrhyw un arall yn y Siambr hon yn ystyried ei fod yn llwyddiannus. Ac rwy'n gwybod bod hynny'n rhywbeth anodd iawn. Wrth gwrs, mae yna bethau y gallwn ni eu mesur; dyna'r pethau ymarferol rwyf wedi eu nodi ynghylch sut y gallwn ni—. Ac mae'n benodol iawn; rwy'n credu bod mwy na 120 o feini prawf achredu y mae Bliss yn mynd drwyddyn nhw. Ond mae hefyd yn ymwneud â sicrhau bod profiad teuluoedd wedi newid yn sylweddol, bod teuluoedd yn teimlo'n rhan o'r gofal. Felly, wrth gwrs, mae'n ymwneud â'r meini prawf y gallwch chi eu nodi ar bapur, ond mae'n fwy na hynny hefyd. Felly, diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Talking of babies and local support, Deputy Minister, Cerebral Palsy Cymru is based in my constituency, and I recently had the privilege of visiting the centre in Llanishen and seeing first-hand the specialist support that they provide to children and families. And I've since received a really moving letter from Glenys Evans, one of the founding parents. Thirty-seven years ago, Glenys and a small group of parents helped establish this charity because they wanted better specialist therapy for their children. Her son, Thomas, who has cerebral palsy, is now 42, and she remains just as passionate as she was then about making sure that the next generation gets the very best start in life.

Now, this is also an organisation whose values have previously been recognised by the Welsh Government, including receiving capital support towards the purchase of their current home in 2019. Now, Glenys has raised concerns with me about the charity's financial future, and changing health board commissioning arrangements specifically. And, at the heart of this, I think, is something that we've all really shared here today, and it's really important, about early intervention and that specialist support can make that real difference to children and their families.

So, Deputy Minister, building on the previous Welsh Labour Government support that was there, how can the new Government work with health boards and Cerebral Palsy Cymru to secure sustainable, equitable access to specialist cerebral palsy support for children and families across Wales regardless of where they live?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wrth siarad am fabanod a chymorth lleol, Ddirprwy Weinidog, mae Cerebral Palsy Cymru wedi'i leoli yn fy etholaeth i, ac yn ddiweddar fe ges i'r fraint o ymweld â'r ganolfan yn Llanisien a gweld drosof fi fy hun y cymorth arbenigol maen nhw'n ei ddarparu i blant a theuluoedd. Ac ers hynny rwyf wedi derbyn llythyr teimladwy gan Glenys Evans, un o'r rhieni a'i sefydlodd. Dri deg saith mlynedd yn ôl, gwnaeth Glenys a grŵp bach o rieni helpu i sefydlu'r elusen hon oherwydd roedden nhw eisiau therapi arbenigol gwell i'w plant. Mae ei mab, Thomas, sydd â pharlys yr ymennydd, yn 42 oed erbyn hyn, ac mae hi'n parhau i fod yr un mor angerddol ag yr oedd bryd hynny am sicrhau bod y genhedlaeth nesaf yn cael y dechrau gorau mewn bywyd.

Nawr, mae hwn hefyd yn sefydliad y mae ei werthoedd wedi'u cydnabod yn flaenorol gan Lywodraeth Cymru, gan gynnwys derbyn cymorth cyfalaf tuag at brynu eu cartref presennol yn 2019. Nawr, mae Glenys wedi codi pryderon gyda mi am ddyfodol ariannol yr elusen, a'r newid o ran trefniadau comisiynu byrddau iechyd yn benodol. Ac, wrth wraidd hyn, rwy'n credu, mae rhywbeth rydyn ni i gyd wedi'i rannu yma heddiw, ac mae'n bwysig iawn, am ymyrraeth gynnar a'r ffaith y gall cymorth arbenigol wneud y gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol hwnnw i blant a'u teuluoedd.

Felly, Ddirprwy Weinidog, gan adeiladu ar y cymorth a gafwyd gan Lywodraeth Lafur flaenorol Cymru, sut all y Llywodraeth newydd weithio gyda byrddau iechyd a Cerebral Palsy Cymru i sicrhau mynediad cynaliadwy, cyfartal at gymorth arbenigol ar gyfer parlys yr ymennydd i blant a theuluoedd ledled Cymru, ni waeth ble maen nhw'n byw?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you so much for raising that really, really important point and for sharing those stories as well, because it is by sharing lived experiences that we need to see where things are going well and where people's lives have been materially improved. So, thank you so much for sharing that.

Evidently—. And I know that you'll appreciate that commissioning is for local health boards, but of course it's something that we're keeping a really close eye on, because Cerebral Palsy Cymru is doing such fantastic work and changing people's lives. So, it's something that we're keeping a really close eye on, and I really value the fact that you've raised that today in the Chamber. Thank you so much.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr am godi'r pwynt pwysig iawn hwnnw ac am rannu'r straeon hynny hefyd, oherwydd trwy rannu profiadau bywyd y mae angen i ni weld lle mae pethau'n mynd yn dda a lle mae bywydau pobl wedi cael eu gwella'n sylweddol. Felly, diolch yn fawr am rannu hynny.

Yn amlwg—. Ac rwy'n gwybod y byddwch chi'n gwerthfawrogi mai mater i fyrddau iechyd lleol yw comisiynu, ond wrth gwrs mae'n rhywbeth rydyn ni'n cadw llygad agos iawn arno, oherwydd mae Cerebral Palsy Cymru yn gwneud gwaith mor wych ac yn newid bywydau pobl. Felly, mae'n rhywbeth rydyn ni'n cadw llygad agos iawn arno, ac rwyf wir yn gwerthfawrogi'r ffaith eich bod chi wedi codi hynny heddiw yn y Siambr. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae'n glir, onid ydy, fod yna gefnogaeth i'r siarter dros y Siambr, a dwi'n falch o ddweud, wrth gwrs, fod y Democratiaid Rhyddfrydol yma yng Nghymru yn ei gefnogi o hefyd. Gaf i jest gofyn: sut ydych chi am sicrhau bod yna weithlu arbenigol ar gyfer y siarter yma? Achos rydych chi wedi sôn am ddarparu gwasanaethau yn Gymraeg, yn ddwyieithog, a dwi'n siŵr ei fod o'n anodd trio recriwtio a chadw staff dros y gweithlu. Felly, a oes gennych chi gynllun i sicrhau bod staff yn y maes yma yn cael eu cadw yn y maes ac yn cael eu recriwtio a chael cefnogaeth hefyd? Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: It's clear, isn't it, that there is support for the charter across the Chamber, and I'm pleased to say, of course, that the Liberal Democrats here in Wales also support it. May I just ask: how will you ensure that there is a specialist workforce available to deliver this charter? Because you've mentioned providing services through the medium of Welsh and bilingually, and I'm sure it must be difficult to try and recruit and retain staff across the workforce. So, do you have a plan in place to ensure that there are staff available in this area and that they can be retained and recruited and receive the support that they need? Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Jane, ac, yn gyntaf, diolch am eich cefnogaeth chi hefyd. Mae fe'n codi calon bod yna feysydd fel hyn sydd yn uno pob person yn y Siambr yma, achos dŷn ni i gyd eisiau sicrhau dyfodol gwell i'n babanod ni. Felly, diolch am hwnna.

O ran gweithlu arbenigol a sicrhau bod y sgiliau ieithyddol, fel roeddech chi wedi sôn amdanynt, ar gael, mae fe'n rhywbeth ar gyfer y byrddau iechyd, iddyn nhw sicrhau eu hunain. Ond dwi'n meddwl bod hwnna yn codi cwestiwn rili pwysig, felly buaswn i'n gofyn i chi—. Pe byddech chi'n fodlon ysgrifennu ataf i, efallai y bydden ni'n gallu cael sgwrs bellach am hwnna, achos mae fe'n rhywbeth dwi eisiau—. Dwi'n ceisio meddwl sut i ddweud hyn yn Saesneg.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you, Jane, and, first of all, thank you for your support. It's heartening that there are areas like this that unify everyone in this Chamber, because we all want to ensure a better future for our babies. So, thanks for that.

In terms of a specialist workforce and ensuring that the linguistic skills, as you mentioned, are available, this is something for the health boards to ensure themselves. But I think that that does raise some important questions, so I'd ask you—. If you would be willing to write to me, maybe we could have a further conversation about that, because that's something—. I'm trying to think about how to say this in English.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I've been contacted by a constituent, Alexia, who has bravely given me permission to share her own personal story. Precious Maya was born at 29+3 weeks last year after fears for Alexia's life. Born on the sub-regional neonatal intensive care centre at Glan Clwyd, the care Maya and her family received was, in Alexia's words, more than they could have asked for. Although living near to the hospital, they were offered accommodation, allowing them to stay close to their daughter, alleviating the stress of travelling and the financial burden of paying for accommodation. However, Alexia is acutely aware that this experience is not typical, and research from Bliss shows that, on average, for every 10 babies on neonatal wards, there is only accommodation for one family. I really, really welcome the eagerness to work with Bliss in terms of family accommodation, but would the Government commit to looking into a review of the current provision of overnight accommodation for parents of babies receiving care, and work with local health boards and Bliss to improve accommodation sufficiency, so that no parent is separated from their baby due to financial constraints?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae un o'm hetholwyr, Alexia, wedi cysylltu â mi ac wedi bod yn ddewr yn rhoi caniatâd i mi rannu ei stori bersonol ei hun. Cafodd annwyl Maya ei geni yn 29+3 wythnos y llynedd ar ôl ofnau am fywyd Alexia. Wedi'i geni yn y ganolfan gofal dwys newyddenedigol is-ranbarthol yng Nglan Clwyd, roedd y gofal a gafodd Maya a'i theulu, yng ngeiriau Alexia, yn fwy nag y gallen nhw fod wedi gofyn amdano. Er eu bod nhw'n byw yn agos at yr ysbyty, cawsant gynnig llety a sicrhaodd eu bod yn gallu aros yn agos at eu merch, gan leddfu'r straen o deithio a'r baich ariannol o dalu am lety. Fodd bynnag, mae Alexia yn ymwybodol iawn nad yw'r profiad hwn yn nodweddiadol, ac mae ymchwil gan Bliss yn dangos, am bob 10 o fabanod ar wardiau i fabanod newyddenedigol, mai dim ond llety i un teulu sydd ar gael. Rwyf wir yn croesawu'r awydd i weithio gyda Bliss o ran llety i deuluoedd, ond a fyddai'r Llywodraeth yn ymrwymo i ystyried adolygiad o'r ddarpariaeth bresennol o lety dros nos i rieni babanod sy'n derbyn gofal, a gweithio gyda byrddau iechyd lleol a Bliss i wella digonolrwydd llety, fel nad oes unrhyw riant yn cael ei wahanu oddi wrth ei fabi oherwydd cyfyngiadau ariannol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Becca, and I'm sorry again I have to have my back to you when I'm answering, because of where the microphone is. I really appreciate how Members have shared both their own experiences with me and with the Chamber today, and also the experiences of constituents. I really am grateful to all of those constituents too for being willing to have their stories shared. I know that that is no small thing, and you have enriched our understanding, you have enriched our proceedings here this afternoon, and we are all so grateful to you, and we all send our very best wishes to you.

In terms of Alexia and Maya's experiences, of course parents need to remain close to their baby, and that is a key principle of everything we've been talking about. It's a key principle of the Bliss baby charter. Of course, access to accommodation is something that has come up from a number of Members in how it can vary. Claire had raised this as well. It can vary across different services, different parts of Wales, it can create that additional stress and financial pressure for families when they least can cope with that.

As I say, neonatal units are being encouraged to review how they are supporting family presence and participation in care, including practical issues like accommodation, particularly, again, for families who need to travel that extra distance. We as a Government will continue to work with Bliss and health boards and families to understand where those barriers remain—again, I encourage Members to write to me if you see those gaps emerging—and where further improvements might be needed, because no family should face any avoidable obstacle at this most difficult time.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Becca, ac mae'n flin gen i eto bod yn rhaid i mi droi fy nghefn atoch chi wrth i mi ateb, oherwydd lle mae’r meicroffon. Rwyf wir yn gwerthfawrogi sut mae Aelodau wedi rhannu eu profiadau eu hunain gyda mi a chyda’r Siambr heddiw, a hefyd brofiadau eu hetholwyr. Rwy’n wirioneddol ddiolchgar i’r holl etholwyr hynny hefyd am fod yn barod i rannu eu straeon. Rwy'n gwybod nad yw hynny’n beth bach, ac rydych chi wedi cyfoethogi ein dealltwriaeth, rydych chi wedi cyfoethogi ein trafodion yma y prynhawn yma, ac rydyn ni i gyd mor ddiolchgar i chi, ac rydyn ni i gyd yn anfon ein dymuniadau gorau atoch.

O ran profiadau Alexia a Maya, wrth gwrs mae angen i rieni aros yn agos at eu babi, ac mae hynny'n egwyddor allweddol o bopeth rydyn ni wedi bod yn siarad amdano. Mae'n un o egwyddorion allweddol siarter babanod Bliss. Wrth gwrs, mae mynediad at lety yn rhywbeth sydd wedi cael ei godi gan nifer o Aelodau o ran y ffordd y mae'n gallu amrywio. Roedd Claire wedi codi hyn hefyd. Gall amrywio ar draws gwahanol wasanaethau, gwahanol rannau o Gymru, gall greu'r straen ychwanegol a'r pwysau ariannol hwnnw i deuluoedd ar adeg pan na allan nhw ymdopi â hynny.

Fel y dywedais i, mae unedau i fabanod newyddenedigol yn cael eu hannog i adolygu'r ffordd y maen nhw'n cefnogi presenoldeb y teulu a'u cyfranogiad mewn gofal, gan gynnwys materion ymarferol fel llety, yn enwedig, unwaith eto, i deuluoedd sydd angen teithio'r pellter ychwanegol hwnnw. Byddwn ni fel Llywodraeth yn parhau i weithio gyda Bliss a byrddau iechyd a theuluoedd i ddeall ble mae'r rhwystrau hynny'n bodoli o hyd—unwaith eto, rwy'n annog Aelodau i ysgrifennu ataf os byddwch chi'n gweld y bylchau hynny yn dod i'r amlwg—a lle gall fod angen gwelliannau pellach, oherwydd ni ddylai unrhyw deulu wynebu unrhyw rwystr y gellir ei osgoi ar yr adeg anoddaf hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ac yn olaf, Weinidog, Darren Millar.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: And finally, Minister, Darren Millar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Just a couple of questions, if I may. Can I thank you for your statement today? I fully appreciate the ambition that the Welsh Government's got to make sure that all of the centres that we have meet the Bliss standards. One of the challenges we have in north Wales is that we don't have a level 3 neonatal service; we have a sub-regional neonatal intensive care centre. It does some phenomenal work, but we're still having to transfer babies over the border, generally to Arrowe Park Hospital. What work will the Welsh Government do to review the status of that sub-regional neonatal intensive care centre, with a view to potentially raising the standard to make it a level 3 provision for north Wales and, indeed, get people transferred in from over the border rather than the opposite way out? And I would say that it's got some excellent accommodation on site as well at Dawn Elizabeth House, Tŷ Croeso at Glan Clwyd Hospital—a fantastic service.

And secondly, Minister, one of the issues that you and I have visited many times in this Chamber in the past is this issue of baby loss certificates. We know the trauma that people face when they lose a baby and, sadly, at the moment, Wales is the only nation within the UK where these certificates are not available. That's causing a huge amount of unnecessary trauma, and Sands and Bliss and a whole host of other organisations are calling for us to get these things sorted as soon as we can. Can you give us an update?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Dim ond cwpl o gwestiynau, os gallaf. A gaf fi ddiolch i chi am eich datganiad heddiw? Rwy'n gwerthfawrogi'n llawn yr uchelgais sydd gan Lywodraeth Cymru i sicrhau bod yr holl ganolfannau sydd gennym yn cyrraedd safonau Bliss. Un o'r heriau sydd gennym yn y gogledd yw nad oes gennym wasanaeth newyddenedigol lefel 3; mae gennym ni ganolfan gofal dwys newyddenedigol is-ranbarthol. Mae'n gwneud gwaith anhygoel, ond rydyn ni'n dal i orfod trosglwyddo babanod dros y ffin, i Ysbyty Arrowe Park fel arfer. Pa waith y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i adolygu statws y ganolfan gofal dwys newyddenedigol is-ranbarthol honno, gyda'r bwriad o godi'r safon, o bosibl, i'w gwneud hi'n ddarpariaeth lefel 3 ar gyfer y gogledd ac, yn wir, i gael pobl yn cael eu trosglwyddo o dros y ffin yn hytrach nag i'r gwrthwyneb? A byddwn i'n dweud bod ganddo lety ardderchog ar y safle hefyd yn Nhŷ Dawn Elizabeth, Tŷ Croeso yn Ysbyty Glan Clwyd—gwasanaeth gwych.

Ac yn ail, Weinidog, un o'r materion rydych chithau a minnau wedi sôn amdano sawl gwaith yn y Siambr hon yn y gorffennol yw'r mater hwn o dystysgrifau colli babanod. Rydyn ni'n gwybod y trawma y mae pobl yn ei wynebu pan fyddan nhw'n colli babi ac, yn anffodus, ar hyn o bryd, Cymru yw'r unig genedl yn y DU lle nad yw'r tystysgrifau hyn ar gael. Mae hynny'n achosi llawer iawn o drawma diangen, ac mae Sands a Bliss a llu o sefydliadau eraill yn galw arnom i gael trefn ar y pethau hyn cyn gynted ag y gallwn. Allwch chi roi diweddariad i ni?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Gwella Gofal Newyddenedigol sy'n Canolbwyntio ar y Teulu yng Nghymru: Cynnydd tuag at Siarter Babanod Bliss
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Improving Family-centred Neonatal Care in Wales: Progress Towards the Bliss Baby Charter
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Darren. Those are really important questions. In terms of the situation in north Wales and still having to transfer babies across the border, that is something that my colleague Mabon would be leading on, but I'm really happy to have a conversation with him about that, because, obviously, that's something that we need to be taking very, very seriously. So, I'm very happy to take that up with Mabon as the Cabinet Minister.

On baby loss certificates, I'm really glad that this has come up. It's something that, as you know, I feel very passionately about. I want very much for us to be in a position in Wales where we can deliver bilingual baby loss certificates in a way that is safe, in a way that is sustainable. We are looking into how this can be done at the moment. We're in a different situation from England or Scotland, because we don't have our own national records service. And Northern Ireland has decided to go down a different route, where they're not having the same layers of verification. And I want to make sure, and officials want to make sure—and this is what we're looking into—that there wouldn't be unintended consequences from doing something like that. We want to make sure that baby loss certificates are delivered in a way that the right people are getting the right certificates, because, of course, that is so sensitive. But it is something that I pledge to you, I promise, I care deeply about. And so it is something we are looking at very carefully and very urgently. So, diolch, Darren. I really appreciate that you brought that up.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Darren. Mae'r rheini'n gwestiynau pwysig iawn. O ran y sefyllfa yn y gogledd a'r ffaith bod babanod yn dal i orfod cael eu trosglwyddo dros y ffin, mae hynny'n rhywbeth y byddai fy nghyd-Aelod Mabon yn arwain arno, ond rwy'n hapus iawn i gael sgwrs gydag ef am hynny, oherwydd, yn amlwg, mae hynny'n rhywbeth y mae angen i ni fod yn ei gymryd o ddifrif. Felly, rwy'n hapus iawn i drafod hynny gyda Mabon fel Gweinidog Cabinet.

O ran tystysgrifau colli babanod, rwy'n falch iawn bod hyn wedi cael ei godi. Mae'n rhywbeth rwy'n teimlo'n angerddol iawn amdano, fel y gwyddoch. Rwyf am i ni fod mewn sefyllfa yng Nghymru lle gallwn ni gyflwyno tystysgrifau colli babanod dwyieithog mewn ffordd sy'n ddiogel, mewn ffordd sy'n gynaliadwy. Rydyn ni wrthi'n edrych ar sut y gellir gwneud hyn. Rydyn ni mewn sefyllfa wahanol i Loegr neu'r Alban, oherwydd does ganddon ni ddim ein gwasanaeth cofnodion cenedlaethol ein hunain. Ac mae Gogledd Iwerddon wedi penderfynu mynd i lawr llwybr gwahanol, lle nad ydyn nhw'n cael yr un haenau dilysu. Ac rwyf eisiau gwneud yn siŵr, ac mae swyddogion eisiau gwneud yn siŵr—a dyma'r hyn rydyn ni'n edrych ynddo—na fyddai canlyniadau anfwriadol o wneud rhywbeth fel yna. Rydyn ni eisiau gwneud yn siŵr bod tystysgrifau colli babanod yn cael eu cyflwyno mewn ffordd lle mae'r bobl gywir yn cael y tystysgrifau cywir, oherwydd, wrth gwrs, mae hynny mor sensitif. Ond mae'n rhywbeth rwy'n addo i chi, rwy'n addo, fy mod i'n poeni'n fawr yn ei gylch. Ac felly mae'n rhywbeth rydyn ni'n edrych arno yn ofalus iawn ac ar frys. Felly, diolch, Darren. Rwyf wir yn gwerthfawrogi eich bod chi wedi codi hynny.
